items.summary: Google DeepMind and UK government work together to reduce planning assessment times
items.full_text_snippet: How PlanAssist supports officers Routine householder applications account for up to 70% of planning officers’ workloads. They're often simple to approve but take up a disproportionate share of their time. Developed by Google DeepMind in collaboration with the UK government, Google Cloud, and Faculty, PlanAssist streamlines this work, giving planning officers automated support with processing applications and drafting assessment recommendations. First, it validates application documents and architectural drawings, checking that the required information has been submitted so the application can proceed. Next, it checks the application against heritage constraints (such as tree preservation orders), and local and national planning policies. It also checks whether any issues or objections have previously been raised, such as by local residents. Finally, it drafts fully cited reports that can be edited by planning officers before they reach a final decision. Since June, the tool has been piloted across Barnet, Camden, and Dorset councils, and has shown encouraging early results. In addition to more than halving the officer assessment time per application, more than 70% of the reports generated by the tool - including things like whether an application complies with local planning rules, or whether the applicant has submitted all required documentation - were approved by officers with no edits required.

Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates. Building on Gemini 4 Argon , which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward. Our researchers and models are working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster, while strengthening our safeguards in tandem. We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing. Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program . We’re continuing to gather feedback and iterate on guardrails before making Carbon available to developers, businesses, and consumers via our product surfaces as soon as possible. Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at the same introductory price


 as Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.

items.full_text_snippet: Mistral Large 4 (aka Le Chonk) is a multimodal, multilingual, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model from Mistral. It takes text and images as input and generates text. It has about 1T total, 49B active parameter , and a context window of 1M tokens . The model is released in two official variants: FP8 NVFP4 There are also GGUFs created by Unsloth and the llama.cpp team. It’s distributed under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (an MIT derivative that establishes limitations for model-as-a-service offerings). Mistral Large 4 is particularly strong for cybersecurity, coding agents, and multimodality. In this post, we look at how the model works, its capabilities, architecture and more! Table of Contents What is new with Mistral Large 4 Mistral Large 4 combines a large pool of experts with sparse attention and a Pixtral vision encoder. The language model selects a small group of experts for each token, while its attention indexer selects which earlier token positions to attend to. These are two different forms of sparsity, where one selects feed-forward networks, the other selects context positions. You can find all the checkpoints in the Mistral Large 4 collection . Cybersecurity Capabilities Mistral Large 4 scores 82% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index test that asks a model to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch the software. Mistral reports that several closed frontier models score near zero on the same test because they refuse to attempt the work. This is super important for defenders, because fixing a vulnerability usually requires reproducing the vulnerability. In Mistral’s internal testing, Mistral Large 4 was also useful for malware analysis, vulnerability prioritisation and writing detection rules, which the model was not explicitly trained for. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 31 Oct 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Nov 2026 (this version, v2)] Title: Running a 20B Video Diffusion Transformer on Consumer Hardware: A Deployment and Measurement Report for MiniMax H3 on Apple Silicon View a PDF of the paper titled Running a 20B Video Diffusion Transformer on Consumer Hardware: A Deployment and Measurement Report for MiniMax H3 on Apple Silicon, by Zhenzhou (Luke) Shi and 1 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: We report the end-to-end deployment and measurement of MiniMax H3, a 20.38-billion-parameter video diffusion transformer (DiT) - the count measured from the safetensors headers of the Q8 checkpoint as deployed locally (Section 3.2) - running entirely on consumer Apple Silicon hardware: an Apple Mac mini with M5 Pro chip and 64 GiB of unified memory. Using the official bf16-to-Q8 (8-bit, group size 64) quantization path executed locally on the machine, we produced a working text-to-video pipeline with no cloud dependency. We document the full deployment procedure, including two non-trivial blockers and their fixes, and report measured figures for build time, peak memory, and per-clip render latency across four resolution tiers (Draft 384x640 through Native 768x1344). A 15.08-second 576x1024 clip rendered in 4838.49 seconds with a measured MLX peak of 27.467 GiB. We further operated the system as an unattended production pipeline, completing 17 clips in 26.49 hours with zero render failures. A blind human review of the 17 production clips (generation prompts withheld) averaged 3.12, 3.18, and 2.94 out of 5 for structural integrity, temporal consistency, and visible artifacts. All figures in this report are our own measurements except where explicitly labeled as third-party data. This is a systems/empirical report; we make no claim of model innovation. items.full_text_snippet: Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking. For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences. AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast. Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials. Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time. AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours. And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers. VIDEO Shorter Simulation Cycles Change What Engineers Can Explore Accelerated computing doesn’t just speed up individual calculations — it changes how many alternatives engineers can test before committing. Multiphysics simulations model interactions among physical effects, such as heat transfer, electrical behavior and mechanical stress. Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies. “As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. items.full_text_snippet: There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease. The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that. Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet. The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published. C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible. “We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. He described their work as “AI tools built by scientists, for scientists.” The consortium is building a system that harnesses previously untapped Alzheimer’s research data to support scientists’ work. To resolve this tension, we built Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform: full-scale synthetic enterprise environments grounded in publicly available real-world data sources such as O*NET occupational data, online job postings, and SEC filings. The synthetic environments mimic real business workflows, helping Microsoft find issues that generic benchmarks would miss. Safety and privacy are built into the platform by design. Every environment is fully synthetic and automated content-safety checks keep the generated data free of harmful or personally identifiable material. Every day, millions of knowledge workers around the world rely on Microsoft Copilot to draft documents, summarize meetings, surface relevant information, and accelerate productivity. Behind the scenes, this is powered by a network of AI systems, and ensuring they work as intended requires a thoughtful approach to evaluation. At Microsoft, we know that high performance doesn’t come from guesswork. It comes from testing, measuring, and iterating constantly. Healthcare organizations are constantly synthesizing safety signals from across teams so that they can make faster, better decisions that directly influence patient outcomes and regulatory confidence. They may ask Copilot to summarize a meeting and extract action items for their teams. Within seconds, Copilot delivers a structured summary citing specific discussion points from the transcript. A new self-improving framework called ForkPilot learns when it’s worth revisiting earlier decisions to find a different approach and adapts its strategy based on new outcomes. Tested across six benchmarks and leading AI models, ForkPilot measures up to the best existing methods while reducing AI processing demands by up to 59%. items.full_text_snippet: Can you run Linux on the Nvidia RTX Spark laptop? Yes, but it comes with a serious catch. Linux installs and runs on RTX Spark laptops like the MSI Prestige N16 Flip AI Plus, including GPU acceleration through Nvidia’s open kernel driver. The problem is clock speed: once the laptop is plugged into wall power, the GPU gets locked to roughly 780 MHz on Linux instead of the 2 GHz-plus it hits on Windows. That turns a chip capable of around 65 tokens per second on a 120 billion parameter model into one struggling to break 14 tokens per second, for reasons tied to power management firmware that Linux currently can’t read. TL;DR Dual-booting Linux works on the MSI Prestige RTX Spark laptop, with a full desktop, GPU acceleration via Nvidia’s open driver, 4K output at 120Hz, and working audio, keyboard, and touchpad once configured correctly. A hidden Windows-only component called the Nvidia Platform Controllers and Framework manages power delivery between CPU and GPU, and it has no Linux equivalent, which is the root cause of the slowdown. GPU clock speed collapses to about 780 MHz on Linux when plugged in , compared to roughly 2.2 GHz on Windows, because the firmware’s power table is encrypted and only the Windows driver can decrypt it. Benchmarks on GPT-OSS-120B show the gap clearly : Windows hit 65.4 tokens per second, WSL hit 65.1, the Nvidia DGX Spark hit 61, and native Linux on the same laptop managed only 13.9. Memory allocation is a separate headache , since the laptop reserves 96GB of unified memory for the GPU by default and only Windows exposes a setting to change that split, which is required before Linux can see more than a sliver of RAM. WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) is the practical middle ground today , since it rides on the Windows driver stack and keeps full GPU boost whether the laptop is plugged in or on battery, while still running Linux-first AI tools like vLLM. items.full_text_snippet: Today, we’re launching “Polar Peaks”, our third quest in the AI Quests series, created by Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning to teach students how AI works and how to use it responsibly. AI Quests invites students ages 11 to 14 to step into the shoes of Google researchers to tackle some of humanity’s biggest challenges. More than 400,000 quests have been completed to date, localized to 10 languages. Alongside the new quest, we’re also releasing training modules for teachers. Polar Peaks: A journey to map the human brain In the first two quests, students tackle flood forecasting and eye disease detection, inspired by Google Research’s Flood Forecasting initiative and AI model for diabetic retinopathy screening. Our newest quest, “Polar Peaks,” has students travel to the frontiers of neuroscience and see how AI can speed up scientific research.

items.title: Dharma Field Extractor: Any Document In, Structured Fields in JSON Out
items.full_text_snippet: A 2-billion-parameter model that extracts exactly the fields you ask for, from any document type, outperforming every frontier LLM we tested, at a fraction of the cost. In April, we released DharmaOCR-LITE , a model specialized for OCR across a wide range of documents, from contracts and court filings to invoices, IDs and forms. The paper behind it made a narrow, well-measured case for domain specialization: a smaller model trained closer to its task beating general-purpose frontier APIs on that task. OCR gives you the text on a page, faithful to the original formatting. That's exactly what you want when the job is the whole document, like a contract you'll read end to end or a manuscript you're digitizing. However, there's a different use case: you don't want the page, you want specific fields out of it, in a shape a system downstream can consume. Every line item on an invoice, as a list. The patient name, exam type and date from a medical requisition, ready to schedule. The fields off an ID, mapped to the columns of an employee record. Run that document through OCR and you get back everything printed on it, line by line, with no indication of which string is the exam type, which is the date or which number is the total. Someone still has to write the code that maps each value to the right field before it reaches the database. A general-purpose LLM can do this work today, with careful prompting. At frontier API pricing and latency, on a task many businesses need to run at high volume, that quickly becomes the expensive way to solve a well-defined problem. So we built a model for it instead. The Field Extractor takes a document image and either a request for everything it can find, or an exact schema to fill, and returns structured JSON: typed, field by field, nested where the document nests. stories.representative_title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents

factual_summary: 📄 Tech Report | 🤗 Data | 💻 Code We’re introducing StateBench , a benchmark for long-context state tracking —how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve

items.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
items.full_text_snippet: 📄 Tech Report | 🤗 Data | 💻 Code We’re introducing StateBench , a benchmark for long-context state tracking —how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve. State tracking underlies tasks from reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, to following a story as characters physically move around and objects change hands. For example, if a mystery novel states that “John gave Mary the knife” right before a murder occurs, it’s important to know that the state of each character has changed. However, not all state-tracking problems are created equal: some require only finding the latest update; harder ones require following a chain of changes, where one missed step can throw off the final answer. For example, a harder variant of our mystery state tracking would be if John gave Mary the item in his backpack, with it previously known that Edward put a knife in John’s backpack. Transformers have well-documented theoretical limits on hard variants of state tracking with long dependency chains, helping motivate recurrent and hybrid architectures such as Gated DeltaNet that carry a running memory forward. Existing state-tracking tests tend to focus on the hardest cases, but as these designs become more common, researchers need to know which kinds of state tracking each architecture can handle. We would like to understand the differences between architectures not just on the hardest kinds of state tracking, but also on the simpler, potentially more common kinds. To this end, we developed the StateBench benchmark to capture state-tracking problems of different complexity, which we used to evaluate the differences between language models with different architectures. We find that recurrent and hybrid models can generalize much farther than transformers when trained directly on these tasks, while frontier models including Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna still break down on harder forms of...

stories.representative_title: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency

factual_summary: CWE-bench is designed to test the limits of frontier cyber capabilities

items.title: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency
items.full_text_snippet: CWE-bench is designed to test the limits of frontier cyber capabilities. In our continued pursuit to push the horizon at Collinear AI , CWE-bench v2 opens up a public set of 100 tasks that anyone can run and evaluate their models on. The setup is the same as before. An agent gets a checkout of a real open-source repository and a short instruction, with the goal of finding and fixing a security weakness without breaking existing functionality. Scoring is fully programmatic, so results are deterministic and anyone can reproduce them without extra cost. All our programmatic checks have been curated with the help of LLM judge panels that shape them towards the direction of hardness and fairness. We also maintain a held-out set , so that we can keep tracking progress on tasks no model has seen. To evaluate your model on the held-out set, contact cyber@collinear.ai . Our goal is to be exhaustive. A defender has to anticipate the ways an attacker could get in, and get it right every single time. These 100 tasks cover 91 different CWEs, spanning a wide range of vulnerability classes. A model that does well here has to understand the multiple weakness surfaces that a potential attacker can exploit. Recognising a familiar pattern is not enough. As part of our meticulous effort to keep improving quality, for every task we checked that the following questions were true: Does the instruction read like a realistic instruction and not an evaluation setting? Can every graded behaviour be inferred from the instruction? Does the verifier check for correct behaviour and not for specific structure of one fix? Does the starter code fail and the reference fix pass? Does the original functionality still work with the new fix? Do the verifiers fail memorized solutions like the known upstream patch? Every task was also reviewed by hand. Open-sourcing the set is part of the same effort to improve quality. We welcome feedback on any task, and contributions to the public set. Results Result...

items.title: Introducing AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel: Open Models for Speech and Decisions on Apple Platforms
items.full_text_snippet:
Language models can do a lot.
They write, summarize, translate, and call tools.
But they're only a small part of what machine learning can do. Say a customer calls your support line.
First, you want to know what they said (speech recognition).
Then, you want to decide where to send them (decision).
You could hand both to a language model,
but there are models built for each that are
better, faster, and less expensive. In our AnyLanguageModel 1.0 recap ,
we looked at a year of local and hosted models in Swift.
With AnyLanguageModel and swift-huggingface now on their 1.x releases,
we're extending the same approach to speech and decisions:
familiar Swift APIs with a choice of model. Today we're announcing two packages: AnySpeechRecognizer implements Apple's new speech-to-text API with a choice of recognition engine,
including NVIDIA's Parakeet and Alibaba's Qwen3-ASR running locally on Core ML,
and adds speaker diarization to track who speaks when. AnyDecisionModel answers yes-or-no, multiple-choice, and rating-scale questions
with typed results and probabilities.
It derives each answer from the model's probabilities
instead of generating text,
using a model on your device with MLX, Core AI, or llama.cpp,
or a decision model from Jev or Ollama. Both packages can download open models from the Hugging Face Hub
and run them on device. AnySpeechRecognizer Computers have been transcribing speech for decades,
and in the past few years, they've gotten very good at it.
Apple platforms already have an API for it.
macOS 26 and iOS 26 introduced SpeechAnalyzer ,
Apple's new speech-to-text API.
You add modules such as SpeechTranscriber and SpeechDetector to an analyzer,
give it a file or a stream of audio buffers,
and read results from async sequences as they arrive. AssetInventory installs the models,
so your app decides when downloads happen. It's a well-designed API,
but the only engine behind it is Apple's.

items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 2 Nov 2026] Title: Measuring Model-Specific Alignment Drift in LLM-Based Opinion Dynamics View a PDF of the paper titled Measuring Model-Specific Alignment Drift in LLM-Based Opinion Dynamics, by Nata\v{s}a Djurdjevac Conrad and 1 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used as synthetic participants in opinion-dynamics experiments, often assuming that an agent's behaviour is fully determined by its prompt. We test this assumption with a framework in which LLM agents discuss a contested policy issue over repeated rounds while their stance is quantified by a fixed psychometric instrument independent of any dynamics model. Across six LLMs, committed personas are intrinsically stable: in each of the five models tested without peer input, every agent keeps its assigned side for 20 rounds. The observed loss of alignment under discussion is therefore interaction-induced, we call it alignment drift, and model-specific: gpt-4.1 keeps opinion clusters apart, claude-sonnet-5 holds them partially, and gpt-5.6-sol and claude-opus-5 abandon them. Under selective attention, one LLM maintains separated opinion clusters under stance-homophilous attention. Qualitative profiles persist at doubled population and horizon and on a second issue. Such heterogeneity makes the LLM choice a first-class validity variable for social simulation. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 2 Nov 2026] Title: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market View a PDF of the paper titled Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market, by Amir Dehkordi (Independent Researcher) and 6 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) read company news at scale, and backtests suggest that their readings predict stock returns. We ask how much of that predictability survives a test that rules out look-ahead, memorization and selection. We propose OLIVIA, a protocol for such tests: point-in-time inputs with company identities masked, selection on validation data only, an analysis plan frozen by cryptographic hash, and a test period unblinded once through a logged lock. We apply it to AI decision models, non-generative language models that return probabilities for typed questions, reading news about S&P 500 stocks: an open-weights model we fine-tuned on 2024-2025 data, three commercial models and standard baselines. The fine-tuned model's signal replicated on two validation quarters (daily information coefficients 0.055 and 0.065) but fell to 0.020 (t = 1.7) on the blinded January-July 2026 test. The commercial models' readings line up with the overnight move to the open (information coefficient 0.074 to 0.077) but not with the move after it, so the news is priced by the time a trader can act on it at the open. No model can tell over- from under-reaction, and no pre-registered strategy survives costs and a deflated Sharpe ratio. Commercial models identify masked companies in 62% to 74% of cases against a 28% baseline: masking hides names, not companies. The market reads the news first. This motivates the question: how much economic value does an AI system produce per unit of energy? To answer it, we introduce Joules-to-GDP, a framework that measures output dollar value minus AI execution cost per unit of energy, which we call Net Value per Joule (NVJ), and expert time saved per unit of energy, or Time Saving per Joule (TSJ). We then apply the framework to 220 GDPval tasks across 44 occupations. Four findings stand out. First, the most valuable work is not always the most efficient. For example, engineering work such as CAD design yields about 10% more net value per task than software development such as building websites, yet the latter yields about 27% more per joule. Second, defaulting to the most capable model can mean less total value from the same energy budget. Of the five tested models, GLM 5.2 delivers the most net value, $72.27 per task on average, using the energy of about four hours of active laptop use, while Gemma 4 31B achieves 56% of that with 23% of the energy, for 2.5x the NVJ and 2.8x the TSJ. Third, for the same model, NVJ and TSJ vary widely across different accelerators, and adding GPUs can raise energy use for modest gains: eight H100s use 3.2x the energy of one to cut completion time by only 22%, at similar net value. More capable models and more hardware must therefore earn their extra energy with enough gains in output value. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 6 Oct 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Nov 2026 (this version, v2)] Title: MINDSET: Energy-based Memory Evolution for Long Conversational Agents View a PDF of the paper titled MINDSET: Energy-based Memory Evolution for Long Conversational Agents, by Sujato Dutta and 4 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: In conversational memory, a later statement may replace an earlier fact, describe a different context, or be an isolated contradiction. Thus, agentic memory must track what changed over time without erasing what was true before. We introduce MINDSET, a memory controller that makes this distinction through explicit state transitions. It preserves original dialogue episodes and organizes them into versioned schemas. For each new episode, it chooses whether to reinforce a schema, supersede its current state, create a contextual branch, or start a new schema. A local energy score balances coherence, contradiction, historical preservation and fragmentation. Stability rules prevent isolated conflicts from immediately replacing established memory. On a frozen 700-question LoCoMo subset, MINDSET achieves the highest observed answer F1 among six evaluated systems and significantly improves retrieval ranking over LightMem. Without retuning, it obtains 69.23% judge accuracy on all LongMemEval knowledge-update cases, compared with 64.10% for Vector RAG. Two additional answer model backbones using Gemma-4-31B and GLM-4.7 provide further qualified evidence of generalization. These findings support explicit memory-state management as a useful approach to changing conversational knowledge. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 24 Oct 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 30 Oct 2026 (this version, v2)] Title: Can Agentic Code Review Catch Vulnerabilities Before They Are Merged? View a PDF of the paper titled Can Agentic Code Review Catch Vulnerabilities Before They Are Merged?, by Yihan Yang and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM agents have been increasingly adopted for security-focused code review, but existing benchmarks mostly derive the reviewed changes from their later fixes instead of the real-world bug-introducing commits. In this paper, we present SecPRBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating agentic security review on validated real-world code changes. More specifically, we have built an automated agentic pipeline to autonomously harvest, build, and validate massive real-world bug-introducing commits for popular software systems. To ensure precise evaluation, we also adopt LLM-as-a-judge to credit the findings matching ground-truth vulnerabilities. To date, we have collected 265 tasks from nine critical systems, including Firefox, V8, and OpenSSL with millions of lines of code. Across eight frontier models, recall ranges from 32.5% to 78.1%, with Grok 4.6 and GPT-6 sol ranking at the top. Our study also shows that most misses are not simply oversights: in 68% of them, the agent reports on a file that holds the flaw but argues for a different mechanism. Security-focused harnesses also behave differently: OpenAI's Codex Security lowers recall by 8.3 points, mostly by abstaining, while Anthropic's Defending Code harness raises it by 7.7 points, at a higher cost. Natural Language Inference (NLI) models can judge whether a single sentence supports or contradicts a claim, but they struggle when the evidence is spread across several sentences. Conversely, Large Language Models (LLMs) can reason across sentences, but may draw conclusions the text does not support. In this experimental study, we test whether a conservative fusion rule, labeling a claim Support or Contradict only when both models agree and defaulting to Not Enough Evidence otherwise, combines their strengths. These retrieved sentences are then provided to every verification model. We then compare a DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli NLI baseline against Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen3 8B, and Mistral 7B. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 30 Oct 2026] Title: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion View a PDF of the paper titled BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion, by Ruurd J.A. Kuiper and 1 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Unlike autoregressive (AR) models, diffusion language models (DLMs) permit parallel token updates, flexible generation, and bidirectional attention, but leading systems rely on costly pretraining or full-model fine-tuning. We present Build Your Own DLM (BYOD), a generalizable LoRA-only recipe for parameter-efficient AR-to-DLM conversion. Without architecture-specific tuning, BYOD induces diffusion generation in Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B, and Ministral 8B; to our knowledge, this is the first reported AR-to-DLM conversion of a Mistral model. The adapters comprise 4.1-5.8% of final parameters while every base-model parameter remains frozen; each 25,000-iteration conversion needs at most 102.4M tokens, processed in 3.1-4.0 hours on one Google Colab GPU. All four models generate from fully masked sequences, use bidirectional context in a controlled attention test, and retain substantial parent-model knowledge. BYOD-Gemma is the strongest BYOD conversion on our nine-task evaluation, reaching 50.6% average accuracy compared with 51.9% for LLaDA 8B Instruct in the same harness. Open-generation quality at low network function evaluation (NFE) budgets remains the principal limitation: BYOD perplexity is 8.3-11.1 versus 4.1 for LLaDA and 2.2-3.0 for the AR parents when generating 128 tokens in 64 steps. items.title: 让Agent首次拥有“视听双流记忆”：openJiuwen Agent-Memory看懂长视频，关键事件一个不落
items.summary: 长视频记忆精度飙升，问答时延最高降97%
items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 让Agent首次拥有“视听双流记忆”：openJiuwen Agent-Memory看懂长视频，关键事件一个不落 思邈 2026-11-04 10:49:02 来源： 量子位 允中 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号QbitAI openJiuwen AgentMemory 正式上线了多模态记忆能力 OmniMem-Lens ：按秒盲切是记忆碎片化的元凶，按真实事件记忆才是正解——召回精度最高提升 45.7% ，在线问答时延最高降低 97% 。 一个让所有Agent头疼的问题：3小时的视频，怎么“记”？ 在AI智能体（Agent）与多模态模型（VLM）快速演进的今天，我们已经不满足于让Agent处理单一的文本工作了，而是让它干更复杂的活儿。 比如“看完3小时的新品发布会，并找出所有产品亮点”，或者“分析一整天的监控视频，并标记出异常事件”。 然而，现有Agent面对超长视频时，海量信息会瞬间超出其上下文限度，导致处理能力和准确度大大下降。 目前业界的通行做法，是粗暴地把长视频按固定时间窗口（如一分钟）切分成一小段一小段，让智能体分开去记忆。 这种方式如同 盲人摸象 ，给智能体记忆带来了两个致命伤： ① 记忆被切碎——证据碎片化 一段原本连贯的老师讲解，在中间被切断，前半段和后半段被智能体分开处理、分开存储。当用户提问时，智能体只能拿到半个“断章取义”的证据，于是胡编乱造、幻觉频出。 ② 记忆被稀释——证据淹没 一个几秒钟的关键动作，与前后几分钟无关的背景画面强行打包。智能体检索细节时，关键信息被大量噪音淹没，召回精度断崖式下跌。 问题的根源是， Agent是“按秒”在记视频，而人是“按事件”在理解视频。 打个比方，你回忆昨天看过的电影，会按“主角相遇→误会→和解”这样的情节去记，而不是拿秒表每60秒存一段。可现在的Agent，恰恰是拿秒表在记电影。 更棘手的是，市面上大多数视频事件分割方案只依赖 单一模态， 只看画面，或只听语音。可这两条路都会失灵：画面长时间不动时，它看不见内容其实换了议题；没有台词时，它听不到任何线索。 这不是算力不足，而是记忆在切分源头就失去了“焦点”。 OmniMem-Lens：让Agent像人一样“按事件”记忆 为了让智能体像人类大脑一样真正处理长视频，团队在 openJiuwen AgentMemory 0.2.0 版本中正式上线了 OmniMem-Lens（多模态记忆透镜） 能力。 作为AgentMemory针对视频多模态记忆处理的核心技术，OmniMem-Lens开创性地通过 视觉 和 听觉 两条轨迹来理解视频中的事件，并以此完成记忆内容的组织，让Agent的视频记忆第一次真正做到—— 按事件存，按事件取 。 团队对它的定位是：给智能体装上一个懂得“自动定焦”和“分层整理”的 超级海马体 。 它做对了三件事： 按真实事件切、分层存记忆、离线建好在线查 。 视觉听觉联动：像人类大脑一样，按真实事件记忆 OmniMem-Lens给智能体同时装上了“眼睛”和“耳朵”： 眼睛看画面 ，画面切换时判断出变化并标记； 耳朵听语音 ，画面没动但说话人换了话题时，通过ASR语音转录分辨出来。 双证据交叉对焦，长视频被切分在真实事件边界上，智能体对视频的理解从此不再“断章取义”。 三层记忆结构：不同颗粒度分层存，细节回溯与整体理解兼得 用户的每次提问，需要的证据颗粒度可能都不一样。OmniMem-Lens在后台建立了一个三层记忆单元： 要大纲有大纲，要细节有细节，检索时按需取用，互不干扰。 就像一本带目录和索引的书：目录（L1）帮你翻到大致章节，索引（L2）帮你定位到具体某一句话，原文（L0）随时可以翻回去核对。 同时，L1与L2记忆单元完全 文本化与向量化 ，可以无缝接入主流向量数据库——对已有RAG/Agent技术栈的开发者来说，几乎零改造即可用上。 记忆离线建，回答在线查：慢功夫提前做，快响应留给用户 如果每次不同角度的提问，都需要智能体把几个小时的视频重新看一遍，不仅反应极慢，还会消耗巨大算力。 OmniMem-Lens把繁重的记忆整理工作 提前在离线做完 ；智能体面对提问时直接查记忆，做到 秒级响应 ，问什么答什么。 在线检索的链路并不复杂：用户Query先与L1/L2的记忆单元做语义匹配，快速定位到精炼的多模态记忆；只有当明确需要视觉细节验证时，系统才按需调取L0层的精确视频帧。这种“ 轻量级文本索引+延迟调取原始视频 ”的架构，大幅提升了视频记忆检索的效率。 OmniM...

items.title: 国行 Apple 智能上手：这些功能已经准备好
items.summary: iOS 27.3 Beta 带来了姗姗来迟的国行版 Apple 智能，这些细节你值得了解。 查看全文
items.full_text_snippet: 2024 年 9 月 10 日，随着 iPhone 16 系列发布，Apple 中国官网打出了「为 Apple 智能预备好」的宣传语。谁能想到，这一「预备」就是整整 785 天。如今，姗姗来迟的国行 Apple 智能，终于在今天和大家见面了。 按照 Apple 公布的安排 ，首批核心功能将从今天起在最新的 iOS 27.3 开发者预览版中开放测试，并计划于 12 月随 iOS 27.3 正式版推出。首批功能会先在 iPhone 上启用，包括写作工具、照片消除和实时翻译等。同时，Siri 也将正式接入千问和百度，带来更强大的回答能力。 不过，这次通过审批的仍是采用「跑马灯」Siri 界面的初版 Apple 智能。WWDC 2026 上亮相的灵动岛液态玻璃玻璃界面，以及下一代 Apple 智能和 Siri AI 功能，都不在本次测试范围内。 但不管怎样，漫长的等待总算有了结果。因此我们也在第一时间更新了 iOS 27.3 测试版，看看它们用起来究竟怎么样。 哪些设备能用？ 这次 Apple 智能测试版仅在 iPhone 上开放，支持的机型包括 iPhone 15 Pro、iPhone 15 Pro Max，以及 iPhone 16 及之后推出的所有 iPhone，iPhone 16e 和 iPhone 17e 也在其中。至于 iPhone 15 和 iPhone 15 Plus，由于只配备了 6 GB 内存，这次依然无缘。而 iPad、Mac 等其他设备则暂不支持，还需要等待对应的审批。 符合机型要求的 iPhone 想要开启国行版 Apple 智能，只需要满足以下任一条件： 使用国行设备，也就是在「设置 > 通用 > 关于本机」中，「型号」末尾三个字符为「CH/A」的设备； 使用海外版设备，登录的 Apple 账户国家或地区为中国大陆，也就是俗称的「国区 ID」； 使用海外版设备，未登录 Apple 账户，且设备定位位于中国大陆。 满足上述条件并更新到 iOS 27.3 开发者预览版后，设置中原来的「Siri」就会变成「Apple 智能与 Siri」。进入后，点击下方的「打开 Apple 智能」，就能看到获取 Apple 智能的按钮了。 根据 Apple 的介绍，最多需要下载 7GB 的 Apple 智能支持内容，下载完成后也需要等待 Siri 升级和启用，所需时间不固定。好在这次没有等待名单，不用先排队等候开放资格。 根据我的 iPhone Air 为例，更新前 iOS 和系统数据分别占用了 17.01 GB 和 27.14 GB，更新到 iOS 27.3 测试版并开启 Apple 智能后，两者分别变成了 22.69 GB 和 31.59 GB，其中， Apple 智能占用了 5.92 GB。 Siri 跑马灯与第三方模型接入 这次 Apple 智能最直观的变化，莫过于呼出 Siri 时的「跑马灯」效果。不过，除了长按侧边按键用语音和 Siri 交互外，你也可以双击屏幕底部导航条的位置，直接打字与它对话。 模型方面，国行 Apple 智能只有本地模型，用于基础的 Siri 功能、照片消除和实时翻译等任务。至于更复杂、端侧模型无法处理的请求，则会将问题与上下文发送至阿里的千问模型进行处理。 不过，千问扩展并不会默认开启，需要手动启用。你可以前往「设置 > Apple 智能与 Siri」，在下方的「扩展」中点击「千问」，再点击「使用千问」，按照弹出页面的提示完成账户登录来启用。除了用手机号登录已有的千问账户外，你还可以选择「通过 Apple 登录」隐藏邮箱。 启用后，借助 Apple 智能对屏幕内容的识别能力，你可以直接通过 Siri 对屏幕上显示的照片、PDF 或演示文稿向千问提问，并持续进行对话。 通过 Siri 与千问对话的历史记录，也可以在登录了同一账户的千问 App 中查看。此外，千问还会出现在后面要介绍的视觉智能和写作工具中，用于理解画面、回答问题，以及创作图文。 至于数据何时会发给千问，Apple 表示，每次发送请求前都需要征得用户同意。在我的测试中，Siri 每次需要调用千问回答时，也确实都会先询问是否允许，得到同意后才会发送数据。Apple 还表示，通过 Siri 发给千问的数据不会被用于模型训练、营销广告或用户跟踪。 除了千问以外，国行 Apple 智能也和百度进行了合作，不过目前仅限于识图搜索，并不负责 Siri 的问答。 总之，随着大模型的加入，Siri 终于不再是那个动不动就和你说「我在网上找到以下信息」的呆萌机器人，语言理解也有了不小改善。它能更好地理解说话时的停顿和改口，也能结合上下文处理连续提问。比如，一句话说着说着发现自己把时间说错了，就可以直接纠正，不用像以前一样取消对话再从头说一遍。 但...

items.full_text_snippet: 平台：macOS 关键词：视频下载、制作字幕、AI 剪辑 @ElijahLee ：Vimpo 是 macOS 平台的一款视频处理工具，它将视频下载、语音识别、AI 翻译、双语字幕和视频剪辑等功能整合在一起，支持从 YouTube、Bilibili 等上千个网站下载视频，也可以导入本地视频，利用本机语音识别模型生成字幕，再通过大语言模型完成翻译和内容分析。 Vimpo 的视频下载功能基于开源项目 yt-dlp 构建，支持 YouTube、Bilibili、Vimeo、Twitch、TikTok 等上千个网站，在 Vimpo 中只需粘贴视频链接，就可以下载视频并保存到本地。下载完成后，视频会进入统一的资料库，并且除了网络视频我们也可以导入本地文件，支持选择复制到资料库或直接链接原文件。 Vimpo 的核心功能之一是自动生成双语字幕。传统的视频字幕工具通常需要依赖视频原有的字幕，或者将视频上传到云端进行语音识别，Vimpo 则采用了本机语音识别与外部大语言模型翻译相结合的方式，它内置 Whisper 语音识别模型，可以直接在 Mac 上运行并将视频中的语音识别转换成文字，因为不需要上传视频，所以本地方案也支持离线识别。 Whisper 语音识别的准确度受限于模型尺寸和准确度，Vimpo 提供了多种规格的模型选项，在我们下载视频时会推荐合适的模型。我们也可以进入应用的设置 - 语音识别，查看内置模型的大小、速度、准确度，根据自己 Mac 的硬件性能，在识别速度和准确度之间进行选择。默认情况下，推荐的 Large v3 Turbo（压缩版）可以较好地完成识别任务，不过偶尔也会出现错误，比如将 iPhone Duo 识别为 iPhone 2。 生成原文字幕后，Vimpo 就可以调用大语言模型将字幕翻译成目标语言。它支持 OpenAI、Anthropic、Gemini、DeepSeek、通义千问、Moonshot、智谱、MiniMax 等服务，也兼容 Ollama、LM Studio 等本地模型。我们只需要配置自己的 API Key，就可以完成字幕翻译。 Vimpo 对字幕的智能处理功能，包括智能断句、人名纠错、术语统一等，可以让长视频的字幕更加易读。播放时可以同时显示原文和译文，并自定义字体、颜色、位置等样式。 Vimpo 将视频播放界面称为「影院」，在这里我们可以同时观看视频、阅读双语字幕和查看完整文稿。点击文稿中的某句话，播放器便会自动跳转到对应时间点。这种设计让视频观看和文字阅读形成联动。遇到听不懂的内容可以直接通过文稿定位，不必反复拖动进度条寻找。 另一个有意思的功能是 AI 精彩片段识别。比如对于一两个小时的长视频，AI 可以根据字幕内容出分析视频中的重要观点，自动挑选值得关注的片段，并为每个片段生成标题、时间范围和推荐理由。 除了观看视频，Vimpo 还提供了一个面向内容创作者的「工作室」，专业用户应该不会对这个窗口感到陌生。在这里 ，画面、字幕、轨道等功能，都是安装按照视频剪辑应用的布局来的。「工作室」通过按键 I/O 打入点和出点，就可以新建片段，手动将长视频中的精彩内容提取出来，制作成独立的短视频片段。 截至发稿，Vimpo 提供 macOS Beta 测试版本，你可以在 官网 下载，测试期间全部功能免费，正式版本计划采用一次性买断，不采用订阅制。

factual_summary: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from

items.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
items.summary: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
items.full_text_snippet: Anthropic is working on an open source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system, called FlashProve , is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” — a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using. Similar to cryptographic email signatures that let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results. FlashProve could also be used to verify claims by third parties that a specific task was done by an advanced model. “A developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model,” the researchers write. “How can a user verify these claims?” To work, the system requires AI labs to publish a “fingerprint” of each model they release that can later be matched to specific outputs and verified cryptographically. Crucially, the fingerprints don’t reveal a model’s weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves and which closed-model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI keep private. That means labs could publish the fingerprints without giving up their most valuable asset, enabling the system to work with commercial models, too. The system is also designed to be lightweight, so verification could be performed on a local device. As part of the announcement, researchers released a detailed tec...

items.summary: Schools choosing to restrict AI altogether will no longer be able to access Google Search, as AI features are now integrated into the search engine.
items.full_text_snippet: Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on. The tech giant says the change follows consultations with schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers. As a result, Google is revising its approach across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. The decision means that schools choosing to restrict AI altogether will no longer be able to access Google Search, as AI features are now integrated into the search engine. Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” which means that if a school chooses to restrict AI altogether, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” The change raises an issue for schools. Although teachers may not want students to use AI Overviews in Google Search to conduct research or complete assignments, they likely still want them to be able to have access to the search engine to find sources and other learning materials. However, Google Search and its AI features are now inseparable. Given the dominance of Google’s suite of apps in classrooms and the widespread use of Chromebooks, the decision underscores the company’s influence over the education sector. Schools that want to continue to have access to Google Search will have to accept its AI features. “We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition,” Phillips wrote in a blog post . “Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit.” Google announced the upcoming change alongside the launch of Guided Learning in schools. items.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models
items.summary: HN 热门讨论（153 points, 75 评论）by ltononro
items.full_text_snippet: Roy Rinberg (Anthropic), Alex Allain (Anthropic); Alessandro Chiesa (EPFL, StarkWare), Miranda Christ (MIT, RESI), Rahul Dalal (Anthropic STEM Fellows Program, Succinct), Giacomo Fenzi (EPFL), Ben Mayer (Anthropic Fellows Program, MIT), Guy Weissenberg (EPFL) Executive summary When you talk to a friend in person, you have many ways to know it is really them: you can see them, hear them, shake their hand. When you talk to an AI model, you have almost none. A user querying a model today cannot check that the responses came from the specific model that a developer claims is responding, as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream. Judging from the model’s output alone is unreliable, even if it produces high-quality responses. Cryptographic proofs of inference solve this problem: they let a model provider commit to a model and then prove that each response was produced by that model. Such proofs could enable applications ranging from consumer products to internal security, and could contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements. Specifically, we have made progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a “zkSNARK”, which is uniquely fit for provable inference (owing to its strong hiding and efficiency properties). In this post, we share some of that progress, primarily through a system we call FlashProve. A brief technical summary is as follows: Claude has produced improvements on zkSNARKs for inference, building a system that is substantially faster than prior open-source systems. For a large model (Llama 4 Maverick, 400B-parameter mixture of experts), a single H100 GPU generates proofs at around 110 tokens/second, with a proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request, when in 4-bit quantized weights, using integer arithmetic in prefill. This is ~70-95x the GPU time of running the model itself on vLLM, a common open-source librar...

items.full_text_snippet:
Software archaeology · The DOOM study DOOM's DNA How code keeps its family resemblance Forty-three programs are descended from the 1997 release of DOOM's source code. Measure only their
      shape and you can still tell who copied whom, and which translations kept the original blueprint. By Joe Esquibel · 31 October 2026 · Everything on this page is interactive: tap, hover, pick. The 43 descendants we scanned, around the original. Each name is sized by how many functions the program has, from
      the Claude-written COBOL raycaster's 45 to Doomsday's 25,482. Tap one to open it. Strip a program of every name, every comment, every line of readable text. What's left is its
      shape: how long each function is, how often it branches, which parts of the program call which. That shape, it
      turns out, works like a fingerprint. DOOM is the perfect place to test it. When id Software released the game's source code in 1997 (the version known
      as linuxdoom ), programmers started copying it, porting it and rebuilding it, and they have not stopped. We
      gathered 43 of those descendants: faithful copies, souped-up source ports, and translations into about twenty
      languages, from Go and Scheme to Fortran, COBOL and even SQL. Then we fed them to a code-measuring engine that
      never reads the code, and asked it where each one came from. 87% / 35% Chocolate Doom keeps 87% of the original's function names, but only 35% of the code inside them is unchanged 0 to 0.6% of DOOM's shape shows up in Quake, Quake II and Lua. stories.representative_title: 模型谁都买得到，拉开差距的是AI生产力系统

factual_summary: AI的下一程是生产力系统之争

items.title: 模型谁都买得到，拉开差距的是AI生产力系统
items.summary: AI的下一程是生产力系统之争
items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 模型谁都买得到，拉开差距的是AI生产力系统 十三 2026-11-03 19:13:49 来源： 量子位 大模型狂飙近三年，生成式 AI 正在集体撞上一道冰冷的商业现实之墙。 一边是硅谷与各大实验室在 Benchmark 跑分榜上卷得不可开交——今天宣称参数翻倍，明天夸耀多模态指标封神；另一边，则是极度尴尬的商业化剪刀差：绝大多数 C 端 AI 应用深陷“规模越大、亏损越高”的泥潭。 当模型能力差距日趋收窄，单纯靠 API 包装套壳的商业模式已被证实难以形成壁垒。海外 AI 视频黑马 Higgsfield 创始人 Alex Mashrabov 曾断言：“AI 应用正死于自研模型的技术虚荣，控制流量路由才是真实护城河。” 但这仅说对了一半。模型路由解决的是“调用效率”，而未能解决“交付能力”。仅仅摆脱虚荣跑分、在前端做流量分发，依然无法逃脱被底层通用模型“平推”的命运。 面对这场温水煮青蛙式的危机，海马云创始人兼 CEO 党劲峰给出了另一个有穿透力的行业洞察： “消费级 AI 很难挣到钱，放眼全球能做成的只有极少数巨头，真正能落地变现的只有垂直生产力场景。AI 下一程的本质，不是发散的概率生成，而是确定性的系统交付。 模型谁都买得到，真正拉开差距的是算力、Harness（Agent、上下文、工具链）与数据深度咬合的‘生产力发动机’。 没有行业 Agent 与专家轨迹的 AI，终究只是会吐字的玩具。” 海马云旗下的 RunningHub 正是这台发动机系统在 AIGC 领域的具象落地。 SimilarWeb 数据显示，今年 3 月到 9 月，RunningHub 海内外全站访问量增长了 266%，增速在同期主流 AI 创作平台中位居前列；今年 7 月，海马云联合创始人兼 CTO 温健在接受央视《焦点访谈》采访时还透露，平台每月的 Token 消耗量已达9万亿。 拆解海马云的技术路径不难发现，这家从实时云渲染起家的技术平台正在展示另一种解法：比起单纯依赖 API 堆砌的前端应用，一套融合算力、工具链与数据的垂直生产力系统，才是突破应用层同质化困境的核心支点。 算力决定成本底线：决定成本的从不只是模型贵不贵，更是GPU有多少时间在空转 在 AI 应用层，抛开算力谈毛利与商业化，往往是空中楼阁。目前市场上绝大多数纯应用层公司（包括 Higgsfield 们）本质上都是“轻资产”运转：缺乏自研算力底座，极度依赖租用第三方云 GPU 或直接透传闭源 API。 这直接导致了两个致命后果：第一，毛利率极易受到上游算力成本的肆意挤压；第二，面对爆发式的商业化调用，算力成本无法做到物理级压榨。 然而，在音视频图像真实的内容生产流程中，AI 推理与传统的图形渲染是交替发生的生产负载。3D 场景需要渲染，Blender、Unreal 等专业软件运行时依赖 GPU，复杂的视频生成与超分合成更是极其消耗计算资源。传统做法是按照业务峰值给推理和渲染各自囤卡，结果必然是“高峰排队、低谷卡闲着”。 “所以决定成本的不仅是模型贵不贵，Token 只是 AI 生产成本的一部分。对于图像、视频和 3D 生产，真正决定单位交付成本的，是从推理到渲染的整条计算链路能否高效运转。未来 AI 生产平台比拼的，不只是算力规模，更是异构算力规模化组织和运营调度的效率。” 这本账是没有底层 GPU 掌控能力的应用公司立不了的判断，也是海马云天然的基因壁垒。 海马云成立于 2014 年，从实时云渲染起家，《原神》《黑神话：悟空》等游戏的云游戏服务背后，都有它的技术支持；凭借多年积累的 GPU 算力调度能力，它也是国内较早把算力投向 AIGC 的公司之一，如今已经完成了从云渲染服务商到 AI 生产力平台 的身份跃迁。 经过十年在实时云渲染领域的沉淀，海马云在全球部署了 69 个计算节点，拥有 6 EFLOPS 的算力池。海马云的底层逻辑，是从根头上把异构 GPU 进行池化，将十年来在实时云游戏领域积累的“确定性交付与毫秒级调度”能力，直接搬到了 AI 推理上。 在 RunningHub 平台上，同一批 GPU 在不同时段服务图像生成、视频生成和专业渲染等不同负载，由统一调度层根据任务类型、模型大小和时延要求实时分配。这种“渲推一体”的算力调度， 将海马云平台的整体算力利用率推到了比行业常见水平高出 70% 的惊人位置。 对于买单的企业客户而言，这意味着极高的性价比；而对于海马云自身而言，自控算力与垂直后训练模型的结合，让其综合毛利率能够稳定站在行业的高位...

items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 纯语音Personal Agent来了！或许，这就是乔布斯心中的Siri Jay 2026-11-03 14:55:30 来源： 量子位 Jay发自 凹非寺 量子位|公众号QbitAI 乔布斯心中的Siri，这次可能真的走进现实了。 长这样子—— 别的先不说，终于来了个审美在线的AI产品，这UI看着是真舒服…… 但大的还在后面。 这语音助手，太魔幻了。 真就跟配了个私人秘书一样，边喝咖啡配面包，边听它汇报今日值得关注的新闻。 关键是真的很有人味啊。即便你中途打断并派给它一个任务，比如「帮我回封邮件」，它也不会陷入尴尬的沉默。 视频来源 简直是电影《Her》里面的 Samantha啊。 就离谱，换做五年前，这样的场景还只能电影院看到。 AI圈打了这么久，每周各大厂商雷打不动瘫软一次，前沿也是花活频出，啥操控Blender、降维机器人、解决千禧难题…… 但坦率地讲， 我一直没觉得这些玩意儿有多让人兴奋 。 离普通人太远了。绝大部分人的现实生活，短期内根本不会因为这些前沿突破发生哪怕一丝一毫的变化。 但我断断续续用了这个产品快一周后，我心里曾经关于AI时代的所有浪漫幻想，突然具象化了。 我甚至觉得—— 这或许就是目前为止，最接近科幻电影， 符合我所有浪漫幻想的AI助手 。 它的名字，叫 Orilo 。 尴尬的Personal Agent Personal Agent这个概念，最近确实被捧上天了。 Muse的增速一度反超GPT，Agent彻底从极客手里的生产力工具，卷向了大众消费市场。 但我说实话，大部分体验真没比年初的「小龙虾」好到哪去。。。 不知道大家怎么样，反正我只有最开始拿到邀请码那几天有点新鲜感，破天荒地给它开了通知权限。 然后，就没有然后了。 打字实在太折磨了。更反人性的是它的主动推送机制，兜里突然震动一下，我还以为是啥紧急微信通知，结果在地铁上艰难地掏出手机一看，是Muse在提醒我一个八百年前就该过期的待办清单…… 我当时就…无语凝噎。 所以我一直觉得，Personal Agent这个市场，至今为止的解决方案仍然都是非常不成熟的。 绝大多数Personal Agent，全卡在同一个致命的死胡同里。我管它叫「一低两高」： 使用频率极低。 不管是订机票还是退订流媒体，听起来确实很酷。但这种复杂任务，你一个月能遇上几回？ 为了这么低频的破事，我还得跟它对齐半天，我为什么不顺手自己点了？ 交互摩擦极高。 你在开车、洗碗、炒菜、跑步的时候，双手和视线全被占得死死的。 这时候兜里一震，让你停下来掏手机打字跟AI盘逻辑，现实吗？ 运行成本极高。 后台每调一次大模型，上面这些场景都需要非常复杂的Tool Call，每一次Loop烧的都是真金白银。 这种成本结构放在消费级产品上，想规模化普及，基本是天方夜谭。 技术原教旨主义统治这个行业太久了。但做个人伴侣这种产品，真不是光靠模型参数大、基准跑分高就能赢的。 下一代能活下来的Agent， 必须能悄无声息、高频地长在生活里 。 语音才是真入口 这也是我觉得，Orilo这个产品，最打动我的地方。 它找到了一个非常符合直觉的新解法—— Voice-first，语音优先。 为啥我说语音对C端产品而言非常非常重要？ 这是人最自然的交互方式。 文字是在语言出现很久之后才被发明出来的，主要用途也是为了知识传递，对日常交流来说其实不是必需品。 你想想，生活中太多时候是不方便阅读文字信息的了，开车、做饭、带娃…… 更重要的是，人在说话的时候，会不自觉地透露出 更多的个人上下文 （Conversational Context） 。 你不会只说「帮我订一张票」，你可能会顺嘴说「帮我订张去上海的票，下周三，上次那个酒店附近就行，对了这次预算紧一点」。 这些「顺嘴」的信息，任何连接器里都找不到，但却是理解一个人的关键。 但这还不够。 语音能打的市场太多了，对于一个新AI产品来说，必须找到一个杀手级应用。 这也是我觉得Orilo第二个很聪明的地方，他们找到了一个刁钻的切入点—— 早晨。 这是人一天当中信息处理频率最密集的场景。 刚睡醒，满脑子混沌，迫切需要知道外面的世界发生了啥、今天这摊子事该怎么安排。 但偏偏，这时候你手里抓着牙刷或者咖啡杯。 Orilo主要针对的，就是这个痛点。 完全解放双手，设备丢到一边， 人只需通过语音接收信息。 在这期间，有任何需要吩咐的事，直接再通过语音向AI输出要求。 泪目了家人们，终于有团队不是坐在人体工学椅上翘着二郎腿、脑补用户痛点了。 而且UI这一块...

items.title: Build specialized multimodal models with LFM3
items.full_text_snippet: LFM3 is our new generation of Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs), built to be the starting point for specialized intelligence. It brings text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models onto one shared backbone, all in the 2B parameter range. This means you can pick the model for your modality, fine-tune it on your own data on a single GPU, and deploy it where your application runs. LFM3 brings four main changes compared to our previous LFM2 family: More capability per parameter: a new tri-hybrid architecture and training recipe allow LFM3-1.7B to outperform LFM2.5-2.6B while using 35% fewer parameters. Every modality on one backbone: six 2B-class models (text, vision, audio, omni, and decision) trained from LFM3-1.7B-Base, including our first omni model and video input for our vision model. Built for the edge: the text model fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit precision, new in-house vision and audio encoders speed up processing, and the text model’s 256K context window lets agents run on-device. Made to be specialized: every model fine-tunes on a single GPU, so you can adapt it to your data, terminology, and deployment environment. How we built a more expressive backbone LFM2 showed that a hybrid of short convolutions and attention can run fast on-device without sacrificing quality. For LFM3, we used our hardware-in-the-loop architecture search to redesign that architecture for agentic use cases, which need more capability per parameter and fast inference over long contexts. The search now covers 14 device and backend combinations, from phones and a Raspberry Pi 5 to laptops, cloud CPUs, GPUs, and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU. LFM3-1.7B-Base has 24 layers and four main changes: Tri-hybrid layer mix: 13 gated short convolutions, 5 sliding-window attention (SWA) layers with a 256-token window, and 6 global attention layers. The convolutions use a kernel size of 7, up from 3 in LFM2. Head-wise gated attention: a sigmoid gate scales each head's output, so a head can switch off when...

items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 机器人干活，AI当厂长！这家巨头要造下一代自主智能仓 梦瑶 2026-11-03 21:57:11 来源： 量子位 梦瑶 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI 具身智能，开始挑战更复杂的生产场景了。 当一众厂商还在围绕拣货、家务等任务探索时，如今有玩家盯上了具身智能产业化的一块硬骨头： 智能仓储 。 而且野心不小，要让AI接管整座仓库，实现7×24小时自主运行，还能在真实业务中持续学习、自主进化。 这个玩家的名字大家也不陌生，正是全球智能机器人的头部企业 「极智嘉」 （Geek+）。 就在最近，极智嘉正式亮出《24/7自主智能仓计划》，目标直指物理AI时代的自进化智能仓。 从让具身AI真正干活，到让整座仓库自己运转，物理AI这次直面的，是产业化更深层的考题。 从会干活到会自己管，物理AI开始挑战更难的一关 在AI深入工业场景的过程中，其实一直藏着一个蛮尴尬的事实—— 物理AI的自动化程度越高，对人工的依赖反而越集中在最难的环节。 过去十多年，AMR让搬运、存储等大量标准化作业实现自动化，货物甚至能自己找到人。 可一旦进入复杂拣选，面对成千上万种SKU、频繁变化的包装和摆放位置，机器人依旧容易犯难。 这也暴露出仓储自动化长期以来的一道瓶颈：单点效率的提升，已经很难支撑整座仓库的智能化跃迁了。 也正是在这个节骨眼上，极智嘉对下一代仓储智能化的突破口，给出了自己的行业判断： 下一代仓储智能化的关键，是实现7×24小时自主运行、持续进化，并依托全球规模化商业能力，让自主智能仓成为新一代生产力基础设施。 这一判断背后，其实藏着仓储行业越来越现实的一笔经济和技术账。 对客户来说，仓库每多一小时自主运转，就意味着多一小时摆脱 人工班次限制 的产能。 尤其在夜间和订单高峰，持续稳定的履约能力，直接关系到供应链的响应速度。 更重要的是，能让投入重金的自动化设备真正跑满产能，把夜班用工、现场管理的压力转化为实实在在的 运营收益 。 但这就意味着，机器人要能处理从未见过的异常，而且整仓系统要能在数百台设备同时运行时自主决策、故障恢复、积累经验。 毕竟，只有整座仓库具备自主应对不确定性的能力，技术上的自主智能，才能真正转化为 商业上持续、可衡量的生产力 ～ 基于这一判断，极智嘉提出的《24/7自主智能仓计划》则将全仓自主化作为下一阶段的战略方向，分三步推进： 打通全流程： 让具身智能接手复杂操作，补齐仓储作业中长期依赖人工的环节。 强化智能闭环： 让AI从发现问题走向自主决策、动态调整，推动整座仓库越干越聪明。 规模化落地： 凭借全球交付与本地化运营能力，让自主智能仓真正走进更多商业场景。 而这三个方向，恰好对应着物理AI规模化落地必须跨过的三道坎—— 机器人能不能独立完成复杂作业、整座仓库能不能自主决策、这套模式能不能大规模复制。 这套庞大的系统性能力，事实上如今也早已在这家公司多年的技术积累与商业化实践中，长出了真实立体的形状。 机器人长手脚，AI接管大脑，无人仓开始自主进化 具身智能解决方案，让机器人干真活 要让一个仓库真正自主运转，那就首先要解决一个基础的问题—— 机器人能否打通端到端的物理作业链路，让自动化从单点突破走向全流程贯通。 单个机器人能干多少活，决定的是单一作业效率上限；整条作业链能否自主闭环，决定的才是无人仓的落地深度。 相比聚焦单机或特定任务的具身智能方案，深耕具身十余年的极智嘉，在真实落地的能力上显然有更深的家底。 其自研的Gravity统一具身智能框架与Gravity 4D具身世界模型，瞄准的正是机器人在复杂环境中的自主操作难题： 前者让机器人理解任务、规划动作，学会先想清楚再动手，后者则让其理解物理空间的几何关系、受力与接触变化。 两者结合，让机器人在面对复杂任务和突发变化时，有了更多自主应对的能力： 跨任务泛化： 面对不同材质、形状的陌生物品，不用逐个训练，也能判断怎么抓。 动态抗干扰： 物品突然移动、被遮挡，也能及时调整动作，继续完成任务。 长程任务执行： 面对多步骤复杂任务，能够自主拆解、规划并逐步完成。 自然语言纠偏： 动作出现偏差，不用重新编程，通过语言指令就能调整策略。 此外，基于多模态感知、长程任务推理、4D物理建模与动作规划等能力，机器人如今也开始走进了真实仓储作业。 比如其通用人形机器人 Gino 1 ，既能拣货、搬箱，还能与移动机器人协同，完成连续的拣选任务： 另一边，极智嘉的 无人拣选工作站 ，也开始接手过去高度依赖人工的拣播环节。 在施耐德电气上海物流中心...

items.full_text_snippet: Matrix 首页推荐 Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。 文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。 按 CodexBar 的统计估算，这一次重做微诗，我烧掉了近 2 万美元的 token。这还没算上 Suno 生成音乐、TTS 合成朗读、OSS 存储和服务器的费用。 没有融资、没有收费，也没有什么商业计划。花这些钱，只是为了把一个自己喜欢了很多年的东西做成自己心里的样子。 故事要从十年前说起。 2015 年 1 月，我做了一个小 App，叫「微诗」，上线时在 V2EX 发帖和大家分享过。那时候它支持 iOS 8，内置了全唐诗和全宋词的数据库，可以离线搜索。功能谈不上多，界面也朴素，但那是我第一次把自己的爱好，做成一件可以拿出来和别人分享的东西。 十年过去了。这中间它被搁置了很多年，我也几乎以为它会就这样留在旧硬盘里。今年我从零开始把它重写了一遍，用的是 SwiftUI 和 WidgetKit，身边多了几个 AI 编程助手。 这篇文章想和大家聊聊微诗的过去和现在。 把一本诗集装进手机 毕业以后，我去了北京一家大型互联网公司做移动端开发。工作几年手上攒了些经验，心里也慢慢冒出一个念头： 我一直喜欢古诗词，能不能把这个爱好，做成一个有用的小工具，分享给同样喜欢它的人？ 于是有了第一版，它把全唐诗、全宋词装进手机里，不联网也能搜。在那个流量还很金贵的年代，想读的时候随手就能翻开算得上是个亮点。上线以后，我陆续收到不少用户的反馈，印象最深的有两类：一类希望加上注释和赏析，读到生僻的典故时能有个依靠；另一类希望加上拼音，因为很多字认得出形，却不敢确定读音。 后来微诗慢慢有了更多用户，最多的时候有近 10 万人在用它。这对一个业余做的小 App 来说已经远远超出了我的预期。所以在工作之余我依然保持断断续续地更新，前后做了 6 个大版本。这些用户的建议我也一直记着。 可一个人在业余时间里能做的总是有限，很多想法在待办清单里一放就是很多年。 2016 年底，我离开公司出去创业。创业公司里能分给一个业余项目的时间和精力少之又少，我的工作重心也从客户端开发，转向了服务端和公司的技术管理。到 2017 年前后，微诗最终停了下来，就此被搁置。 之后的几年创业失败，我回到了大公司，也经历了一次职业上的转型。生活推着人往前走，那本装在手机里的诗集，离我越来越远。可我心里一直没有真正放下它。 那些曾经用过它的人，那些没来得及做完的想法，时不时还会冒出来提醒我：这件事，还没有做完。 推倒重来 让我重新拾起这个爱好的，是今年 AI 能力的大幅提升。离开客户端开发这么多年，如果要我一个人、只靠业余时间，把一款 App 从头做到自己满意的程度，过去我是不敢想的。 而今年，和 AI agent 一起工作，这件事第一次变得可行了。 十年间，iOS 和 Swift 本身都已经变了太多，与其在旧代码上修修补补，不如重新开始。我最后的决定是从零开始，一行旧代码都不留。技术栈也很快就定了下来：界面全部用 SwiftUI，小组件用 WidgetKit。小组件本来就只能用 SwiftUI 写，主 App 和小组件共用一套视图和数据层。对一个人维护的项目来说，这样的组合是最省心的选择。 新的微诗，我给定下了三个词：美观、简洁、诗意。我希望它是「装在手机里的一本诗集」，是一本你愿意偶尔翻开、翻开之后不会被打扰的书，在微诗里，诗不只是用来默读的——它可以被朗读，可以被吟唱，也可以化作一幅画。 新版微诗 打开微诗，首页是当天的一首诗。这首诗的选择会跟着二十四节气走。 我很喜欢这种安排。节气本身就是古人写给时间的诗，立春、清明、白露、霜降……用诗来标记日子，比一个冷冰冰的日期更像生活本来的样子。 放在锁屏上的「诗笺」小组件是我自己用得最多的功能。每天拿起手机看时间的那一下，顺便看到一两句诗，不需要打开 App、不需要做任何事，它就在那里。 锁屏小组件的空间非常小，而且系统会以单色方式渲染，能用的只有字形、字号和留白。在这么小的一方地方里，让一两句诗读起来仍然舒服，是我反复琢磨过的事。 新版微诗里还有一组动态壁纸：山水是一笔一笔画出来的。我想要的效果是像看一个人在纸上作画，而不是看一段特效，速度太快就没了意境，太慢又让人失去耐心，分寸全在一点点调出来的节奏里。 古人的诗，很多本来也是用来吟、用来唱的。只用眼睛读，总觉得少了点什么。所以这一版的微诗中，诗不只可以默读，你可以听它被朗读出来（TTS），也可以听它被唱出来——这些曲子是我用 Suno 一首一首做出来的。 第一次听到一首熟悉的诗被唱成歌的时候我发现，字还是那些字，却好像换了一种方式走进了...

items.title: Disc Image Studio：你想不想在光盘上「画」点什么？
items.summary: 把喜欢的图烧进 CD 里，你也可以。 查看全文
items.full_text_snippet: Matrix 首页推荐 Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。 文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。 前段时间出于某些契机，在GitHub上认识了 这样 一个有趣的项目，它支持你利用 任何刻录光驱 与 任何光盘 在数据区刻录出肉眼可见的图案。 老资历应该一瞬间就能想起来，在光盘上「画图」的技术其实挺早就有了： 2002 年雅马哈的 DiscT@2 技术允许在 CD-R 的数据面烧图，但必须使用专用刻录机。 2004 年惠普的光雕（LightScribe）和 2005 年雅马哈与富士胶片的闪雕（LabelFlash），允许把图案刻到标签面；老实说挺好看的，但必须使用专用刻录机配专用涂层盘，巨贵，还得手动把盘翻面再刻一次，多花很多时间。 这三个技术很快就寄了，专用盘和光驱陆续停产，现在这些设备都挺贵的。 但这个开源项目 Disc Image Studio 极其炫酷：只需要普通刻录机 + 普通空白 CD、DVD 或单层 BD-R，通过一些算法把图像信息转为数据，再把它写进数据区。放在台灯下看数据面就能看到图案了。 太高雅了，特写此文，同各位分享刻一张图的流程。 大概的原理 为方便大家理解后面的刻录与标定流程，先简单介绍下项目的原理。 光驱在光盘上烧录数据时，激光在盘片上留下微小的坑点（或变色点），两者的反光不同，光驱读到亮暗变化就是 0 和 1。很明显，宏观上，这些坑也可以呈现出光学性质。这就是在数据区刻图的原理。 刻录时，光驱头从中心向外沿一条螺旋轨道走。以 DVD 为例，数据区在内半径 24 mm 到外半径 58 mm 之间。 光驱处理数据时，数据将被切成固定长度的扇区：一个 DVD 扇区约 5.16 mm，全盘固定 2,297,888 个，所以整条轨道的总长度也是固定的。每个扇区在盘面上的位置——半径加角度——由内外半径和轨距（相邻两圈之间的距离）共同决定，这就是地址表。 基于如图演示的这套流程，Disc Image Studio 将最终生成一段数据，刻录上去即呈现出图案。 所以在这套方法里，图像是「一圈一圈印上去」，沿螺旋一路采样铺开的。只要 地址表里的内外半径和盘片真实尺寸一致 ，每个像素就会落在该在的位置。 但这实际上成了最难的一步：光盘尺寸虽有国际标准，但光盘毕竟本不是用来画画的，每个厂家每个型号光盘的真实内外半径与扇区数都是有细微差别的！ 一张参数正常的盘面。 差了会怎么样 写这篇文章的主要目的就是教大家如何计算标定每个型号光盘的真实物理参数，所以让我们先看看当参数不准确时，会发生什么。 地址表是按软件以为的半径算的。盘片的真实内外半径只要差一点，同一个扇区实际落下的角度，就会和软件预期差一点；偏差不断累积，越靠外错得越多。 沿用第一节我们展示的标准图案，这套数据生成时采用的参数是内半径 24 mm、外半径 58 mm。现在我们分别模拟一张内半径实际情况为 24.002 mm 和 24.05 mm的光盘，看看印上去会呈现怎样的图案： 差 0.002 mm：图案已经明显扭曲，但还能看出大致格局。 差 0.05 mm：成为螺纹，原来的图已经看不出来了。 按 DVD 的螺旋几何估算，内半径差 0.002 mm 时，外圈累计的角度偏差约为 1.1 圈；差 0.05 mm 时约为 28 圈。 所以接下来就进入我们正式的印刷教学了。 最省事的办法 实话实说，没有经验，初次标定需要花上几天，报废 10 ~ 30 张盘。 所以如果你不打算在标定上花时间，只是想刻几张玩玩或者送朋友，最简单的做法是买作者已经标定过的型号。软件内置了几个实测过的预设参数，新建工程时直接选就行了： DVD ：Verbatim DVD-R AZO（43533） CD ：铼德医疗水蓝盘、Verbatim CD-R AZO（43438） 蓝光 ：铼德 BD-R 10x、Verbatim BD-R（64099） 买盘时务必认准型号、产品编号！同一个品牌的不同型号、不同批次，参数不一定相同。就算你确保买对了，也建议先刻一张测试图看看效果。 手工标定-粗调 如果你下定决心想自己标定自己手上的盘，那就开始吧！ 做第一张标定图案并刻录 这张图只用来观察，好不好看无所谓，主要是要方便辨认。 贴近外缘 ：图案放在靠外的位置。偏差从内圈开始积累，到外圈最大，放在外面容易看出来； 径向要长 ：每条黑线从靠外处向里延伸一段，以方便看出被拧弯的弧度； 在圆周方向铺开一部分 ：一组线沿盘面外缘排开，才能容易看出螺纹是顺时针还是逆时针，判断该往哪边调； 黑白分明、间距固定 ：边缘要清楚，方便看。 前文的示例用了一组从靠外处向里伸的黑色短横条...

factual_summary: Ask a frontier model for a slide deck and you'll get a good one

items.title: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
items.full_text_snippet: Ask a frontier model for a slide deck and you'll get a good one. Ask for ten and they start to look alike: the same tasteful defaults, the same house style, a faint "AI-generated deck" look. That's fine until you want the deck to look like your template. Frontier models have their own house style, and no amount of prompting stops them drifting back to it. And sometimes the content is confidential and can't leave your systems at all. Both of those point to a model you own: open weights, running on your own infrastructure, trained on your own design language. The catch is that small open models, the kind you'd actually self-host, are bad at this. Their decks come out broken: titles that vanish into the background, text running off the slide, shapes stacked on top of each other. Palette tests one bet: that a small open-weight model, trained on synthetic data in your design language and checked by a harness, can compete with frontier systems while you keep ownership of the result. We fine-tuned a 20B model to build decks the way people do: a designer plans the deck and a coder draws each slide. Its training data follows the IBM Design Language , and on PresentBench it ranks first on two of the three domains we measured. This post covers how we synthesized the data, trained the model and built a harness around it. Why decks are hard for small models A slide deck looks simple, but making one asks a model to do three things small models are bad at. It lays out the slide without seeing it. The model doesn't draw slides; it writes code that places every element at an x, y, width and font size. Whether a 75-character title fits on two lines at 56pt is arithmetic the model does in its head, and it only finds out it was wrong after the code renders. Small models get this wrong often, which is where overlapping shapes and text running off the slide come from. It makes two kinds of decisions at once. items.full_text_snippet: An initiative bringing together universities, research organizations, industry, and the open science community to make publicly funded research easier to discover, reuse, and build upon. Today, we're announcing Project ProtoStar , an initiative to unlock the potential of publicly funded scientific research by making datasets, models, and code more accessible and reusable, particularly for AI-driven research. ProtoStar brings together research institutions, industry, and the open science community to support the release of scientific artifacts in AI-ready, machine-actionable formats, and to demonstrate their value through a series of open challenges. The first challenge, hosted by Carnegie Mellon University , opens on November 2. See How to Participate below. The initiative's founding partners include Carnegie Mellon University , Purdue University , Georgia Institute of Technology , Arizona State University , and The George Washington University , all working through the Open Forum for AI (OFAI) as the university coalition partner; the Astera Institute ; Hugging Face as the infrastructure partner; and the Open Research Community Accelerator (ORCA) , through its Fostering Innovation Network , as the community partner. Participating organizations formalize their involvement through a memorandum of understanding supporting the release of suitable scientific datasets, models, and code in AI-ready formats on open infrastructure. Organizations interested in joining Project ProtoStar can reach out to protostar@orcaopen.org . Making publicly funded science more usable The U.S. federal government invests approximately $190 billion annually in research and development , and federal policy increasingly expects the results to be shared publicly. items.full_text_snippet: OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane thinks the 2028 presidential election could be a defining moment for AI. And he wants politicians to start developing policies that address Americans’ concerns about the technology, rather than simply paying lip service to anti-AI sentiment and the backlash against data centers . In a new essay , Lehane compares AI’s potential to reshape the economy to President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal, the 1930s set of federal programs and reforms enacted after industrialization and the Great Depression shattered the old economic order. He observes that Americans today feel similarly anxious about losing control over their economic futures and urges politicians to find a “compelling third path” that allows people to share in AI’s benefits. He lays out five policy priorities, spanning worker protections and education to AI safety and data center development. The essay comes on the heels of a stunning Democratic victory in the midterm elections, in which Democrats flipped control of Congress amid widespread voter frustration over the cost of living. Kate Brennan, who leads AI and corporate power policy at the AI Now Institute, told TechCrunch that Lehane’s rhetoric marks a notable shift from OpenAI’s policy agenda last year, which focused on accelerating AI development, reducing regulatory barriers, and expanding infrastructure. Unsurprisingly, many of Lehane’s proposals would encourage wider AI adoption and support the infrastructure expansion companies like OpenAI need to grow. The original New Deal established protections for workers and placed constraints on corporate power. It’s less clear how Lehane’s vision would hold AI companies accountable for the economic disruption their technology could create. “Invoking a New Deal metaphor is to invoke state capacity to actually benefit the public,” Brennan said. “This is written by a private company that is trying to advocate for policies for its own benefit. items.full_text_snippet: Meta has acquired Conductor , an AI coding startup that allows users to spin up software projects by deploying multiple agents into parallel workspaces. The news was originally reported by Axios, and Conductor shared news of its acquisition on its blog. “I have big news: Conductor is joining Meta,” wrote the startup’s founder and CEO, Charlie Holtz, on Wednesday. “We have some big, crazy plans for the next interface,” he added, teasing that the company would have “something new” for customers to use by “early next year.” On X, Holtz also noted that he was looking forward to working with Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, and Nat Friedman, head of product at the company’s Superintelligence Labs. “They’ve been on an absolute tear, and I’m convinced MSL has the highest talent density of all the labs,” he added. Meta confirmed the acquisition to TechCrunch but wouldn’t comment further or provide additional details about the deal. Conductor, founded in 2024, only launched its core product just last summer. The company’s agentic teams, which can be deployed in the cloud, locally, or via a user’s phone, are designed to help software engineers work on separate, compartmentalized parts of a project in concert. The agents that the platform deploys aren’t developed in-house but come from major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Holtz said that, until early next year, Conductor’s core features would continue to work as they previously have. The exception is Conductor’s cloud service, which will shut down on November 20, after which the company will begin deleting user cloud data. Meta, which previously lagged behind in AI services, has spent the last several months trying to catch up. In August, the company launched Muse Code , its own coding agent. items.summary: HN 热门讨论（215 points, 128 评论）by ersinesen
items.full_text_snippet: This is a guest essay by Jessica Hullman , Ginni Rometty Professor of Computer Science and Policy Fellow at Northwestern University. Diego Velázquez, The Fable of Arachne (c.1657) In his essay on the role that rigorous proofs play in mathematical advances, Bill Thurston writes that the measure of success in math research is “whether what we do enables people to understand and think more clearly and effectively about mathematics.” Many recent discussions of AI for science hinge on a tension between understanding and answers. Is science about humans achieving insight, or the archiving of verifiable solutions? One side prioritizes outputs. Progress is implied to be evident in verifiable proofs of longstanding conjectures and cures for diseases, whether humans were involved in their making or not. The other side argues that human understanding is paramount, because it drives integration of new findings into the canon, because it shapes and inspires the next generation, and so on. But the first side, those who emphasize correct outputs, dismisses this as gatekeeping or nostalgia. When Terry Tao posed a thought experiment in a recent talk , asking how comfortable people would be taking a cancer treatment produced by AI, complete with a formal certificate of correctness and a passed phase 3 trial, but without any human understanding how it was found, critics suggested that Tao’s reasoning missed the point. Of course a patient with stage 4 cancer would welcome the treatment. Other examples concern ambiguity in authorship. Tom Dietterich wrote about arXiv’s growing problem with papers submitted by human authors who seem unlikely to have the expertise to understand the claims. Many questioned in response why accountability – by which I mean being answerable for a claim, able to describe what it rests on and respond when it’s challenged – should matter if verification has been solved. items.full_text_snippet: 发现不少小伙伴很好奇我是怎么用 Mac 来开发 Windows 软件的，以及 Windows 软件现在一般用什么技术栈来实现，刚好我这段时间也在做类似的事情，来和大伙随便聊聊关于多端技术选择的思考。 Web、跨端还是原生 做过前端客户端的小伙伴应该都知道，这些年端的开发一般是这三条路。 第一种最简单方便的是，直接写 Web 代码，塞到浏览器就能跑，包括早年的 PhoneGap、Cordova 就是把网页塞进一个原生壳里，然后提供一些 bridge 的能力让 JS 可以调用到一些原生的能力，比如唤起手机摄像头这类的 Web 不好做的事情。 第二种是跨端开发，也就是早年大家常听到的一码多端。当时移动端有 React Native、Weex 这一类技术，主要是为了解决 Web 性能差的问题，一份代码同时打包 iOS 和 Android。国内大厂当时重度用跨端还有一个非常大的原因，就是动态化和热更新，讲得土一点就是可以绕过商店审核直接下发新页面，这也是国内跨端在移动互联网高速发展时特别流行的重要原因。 桌面端大家熟悉的就是 Electron，现在不少 AI 桌面端、VS Code、Slack 是用这个做的，代价是相当于每个应用都自带一份 Chromium 和 Node.js，安装包 100 多 MB，内存也占得多。但好处是在 Chromium 渲染引擎的统一下能够很好地保持多端的展示一致性，加上里面写的代码非常好写，后续不少桌面的速成就会用这个技术。 跨端后面也慢慢延伸出更多有趣的解决方案，类似 Flutter 自己实现一套渲染引擎，早期靠 Skia，现在换成了自研的 Impeller 渲染引擎来保障多端一致和性能效率的均衡，包括桌面端上老牌的 Qt，和 Flutter 一样自己画界面。 这两年桌面跨端也出现了用 Rust 写的 Tauri、Go 写的 Wails，它们和 Electron 不一样的地方就是，没有塞一个 Chromium 进去，而是使用系统自带的 WebView，包会小非常多，但是整体还是基于 Web 这一套研发思路和对应实现语言去进行桥接交互，但是由于系统 WebView 每个平台不一样，Windows 上是 WebView2，Mac 上是 WKWebView，Linux 上是 WebKitGTK，所以多端显示的一致性反而不如 Electron，还是要写兼容代码。所以这种情况下，即使 Electron 很大内存占用也不低，还是会被选择更多。 第三种是原生开发，也是没有 AI 之前大家觉得难度最大的一种方式。早年苹果系的 Objective-C、Android Java、Windows C++ 和 C#，都需要花很多时间去学习、看书、手编代码，深入研究系统底层原理，才能写出性能更好、更稳定的代码，属于前期投入大、后期用户很享受的技术。我 17 年那会儿刚工作不久，职业发展比较爽的一个很大原因，是抽了半年时间学习 Objective-C 和 iOS 研发，让本职是前端的工作提前往跨端方向走了，刚好可以解决一些只懂前端或只懂客户端都搞不定的难题，那也是我做一线开发非常快乐有趣的一段时间。 等到后面 Swift + SwiftUI、Kotlin + Jetpack Compose、C# + WinUI 3 慢慢出来成熟后，这些原生端语言的写法也慢慢向前端的声明式写法靠齐，也更易写了，声明式代码更短、更好读了。但是在国内，原生完全被 React Native、Flutter、Electron 的广泛使用盖过去了，开发者不多，生态发展完全靠官方推动，这也是为什么很多 App 出活很快，但大家普遍觉得用久了卡卡的，而且这类 App 还占了大头。想迁移到原生的话，假如之前架构实现得不好，大概率只能重写，完全不能复用，实现得好，比如你早就把业务逻辑抽出来了，类似 Kotlin Multiplatform 这类方案把业务逻辑共享、界面各写各的原生，算是第四条路，也是最近几年的趋势。 聊到这里大家应该大概明白了，这里也有一个不可能三角，就是研发效率、体验、性能这三者，选择 Web 是多效率少性能，选原生是多性能体验少效率，选跨端刚好是在这三者取一个中间，做得好容易都占，做得不好，容易没有一边占到好处的尴尬局面。 研发效率、体验、性能的不可能三角，Web 靠近效率，原生靠近体验和性能，跨端取中间 那么在现在 AI 写代码不是大问题的情况下，该怎么选呢？很多时候还是看场景。如果是重内容的浏览、阅读这类轻应用，直接用 Web 技术最省心；但如果是需要深度调用系统底层能力，或者追求更低内存和更顺手交互的应用，我依然更推荐原生技术，可以第一时间享受到系统官方本身的众多调优。有了 AI 之后，一个人写两套原生的成本其实大幅下来了，效率那一边被补...

stories.representative_title: 一眼的熟悉，满眼的惊喜：新款 iPad mini 首发体验

factual_summary: 更轻、更薄、更好「看」，依然是那台纯粹的 iPad mini

items.title: 一眼的熟悉，满眼的惊喜：新款 iPad mini 首发体验
items.summary: 更轻、更薄、更好「看」，依然是那台纯粹的 iPad mini。 查看全文
items.full_text_snippet: 在 Apple 的产品中，名字里带有「mini」的产品似乎总有些特别。 方方正正的 Mac mini 别看小，但很能装：高性能芯片、丰富的接口，还能时刻在线，它总能安静并可靠地完成各种任务。纤薄小巧的 iPad mini 别看轻，桌面级的性能加上随手可用的便携性，它既是能打发碎片时间的随身屏幕，也是能随时投入专业创作的趁手工具。 也正是这种尺寸与能力之间的反差，让两款产品始终能在各自的产品线中占有一席之地。只是并不稳定的更新节奏，总让偏爱它们的用户格外惦记。好在今年，继全新的 Mac mini 之后，iPad mini 也终于迎来了久违的更新。 一眼的熟悉 新款 iPad mini 的整体轮廓没有发生太大变化，几乎一致的宽高参数，依然是一块可以单手拿住的小尺寸平板电脑，顶部按键继续集成触控 ID，侧边也保留了用于吸附和充电 Apple Pencil Pro 的磁力接点。 虽然宽度和高度的毫厘之差无法令人感知，但在厚度方面可就不一样了。新款 iPad mini 的厚度从 6.3 毫米降到了 5.4 毫米，重量甚至减轻了最高有几乎 40 克之多。 左：iPad mini (A20 Pro)，右：iPad mini (A17 Pro)。 不夸张地说，拿起新旧两代产品的一瞬间，就能感受到这样的尺寸和重量变化带来的差别。 另一个比较明显的变化，是新款产品的屏幕边框收窄了 24%，在机身尺寸基本不变的情况下，屏幕从 8.3 英寸增大到了 8.5 英寸。虽然新款 iPad mini 的边框依然不能算窄，但变化也是一眼就能感知；对于一台经常需要手持的设备来说，我认为保留一定的握持空间不是坏事，单手拿住这台 iPad mini，拇指依然可以自然地落在边框部分，并不会遮挡任何显示内容。 左：iPad mini (A20 Pro)，右：iPad mini (A17 Pro)。 最后是前置镜头，iPad mini 的前置镜头终于在这一代被移到了的机身的长边，与其它 iPad 产品保持一致。对于 iPad 这类形态的产品而言，这样的设计无疑是更合理的，通过智能双面夹等配件将 iPad 横放在桌面，参加视频会议或通话时的画面角度会更加自然，视线也不会明显偏向屏幕一侧。 对了，新款 iPad mini 的智能双面夹在设计和材质方面都有调整。过去的保护盖通过两条折痕被分成三段，折叠后组成一个三角形支架；新款则改用双重面板结构，只在中间保留一条折痕，将保护盖一分为二。虽然折叠结构有了调整，但实际用法没有太大区别，过去支持的各种支架方式，新款基本都能实现。 新的智能双面夹表面也从过去相对光滑的材质换成了与 iPhone 保护壳一样的科技织物，纹理更加明显，手感也多了一点细密的摩擦感。以我使用 iPhone 科技织物保护壳的经验来说，iPad mini 的新款双面夹应该也会更加耐脏，打理起来会省心不少。 你可能会好奇这款双面夹能不能适配旧款 iPad mini，答案是不建议：由于两代机身尺寸存在细微差别，旧款 iPad mini 装上新双面夹后，机身边缘与保护壳会有轻微错位，后置摄像头也无法完全对准开孔。除此之外，从实际吸力来看，新款双面夹正面的磁铁位置似乎也有所调整，用在旧款设备上时吸附会明显偏弱。 满眼的惊喜 如果要选一项最能改变这代 iPad mini 体验的升级，我会毫不犹豫地选择这块 8.5 英寸的 OLED 屏幕。 新款 iPad mini 的屏幕分辨率为 2316 × 1512，依然维持 326 ppi；SDR 最高亮度从上一代的 500 尼特提高到 600 尼特，这样的区别在日常使用中其实不会让你有明显感知，真正拉开差距的还是这款 OLED 屏幕带来的 HDR 显示能力。 上一代 iPad mini 虽然已经能够播放杜比视界、HDR10 和 HLG 等 HDR 内容，但受限于 LCD 面板和最高 500 尼特的亮度，画面仍要经过色调映射，无法完整呈现 HDR 原本的亮度范围。新款 iPad mini 借助全新的超视网膜 XDR 显示屏，显示 HDR 内容时的峰值亮度可以达到 1200 尼特；再加上 OLED 的像素级控光和出色对比度，画面中的灯光、阳光与反射等高光区域能够以更高亮度呈现，黑色背景、电影暗场和照片阴影也终于不再泛着一层灰。 两台 iPad mini 均调至最高亮度、关闭原彩显示。 虽然有不少人诟病新款 iPad mini 的屏幕刷新率依然固定在 60Hz，没有支持最高 120Hz 的 ProMotion 自适应刷新率，但刷新率并不是影响动态画面观感的唯一因素。 OLED 的像素响应速度比 LCD 快了一个数量级以上，像素可以更快完成颜色变化，从而显著减少画面移动时产生的拖影。因此，即使刷新率没有变化，在同样的 60Hz 下，新款...

items.full_text_snippet: 这篇文章是 TDS Studio 在少数派上的第 34 篇文章，依然是全平台首发。 时隔两年，我们又回来写 AirPods 半入耳型号了。在 26 年的苹果秋季 event 上，AirPods 5 给我们最大的印象其实还是主动降噪往千元内的版本上进行了下放，不仅局限于高配版本专属。但无论是没有明显的续航提升还是完全一致的外观模具，都显得这次产品迭代不那么面面俱到。在后面看到首发媒体内容之后，也基本能确定一个问题，即该出现的刀法还是没少、降噪虽然出色但调音评价普遍不高。究竟如何呢？ 我们首发购入 AirPods 5 的标准版，没有赶首发内容期，来带大家看看同样基于 H2 芯片的这次更新是否值得你关注。正好我们手上也买了一套 Freebuds 7，所以本文也会提及一些近两代 AirPods 与它（尤其是降噪层面）的对比。额外，需要感谢读者 The Boy in the Rye 借出他的 AirPods 4 ANC 辅助这篇文章的完成。 包装与配件 | Package & Accessories AirPods 5 的包装依然还是那个白色方形纸盒，跟四代相比只有主图换了个角度而已，没有任何配件。 设计、佩戴表现与声学结构 | Design, Fit & Acoustic Structure 仅从外观上来看，AirPods 5 这一代其实跟 AirPods 4 几乎没有肉眼可察觉的区别，依然只有白色、依然是那个易划伤的亮面塑料、依然是非常小体积的充电盒，你甚至可以把两边的耳机本体对换充电…… 不过这并不意味着什么都没改。 你能分辨出来哪台是 AirPods 5 吗？ AirPods 5 这次虽然两个版本都有一样的主动降噪性能，但是充电盒和耳机电池部分有明显区别，基础版没有盒身的扬声器和无线充电线圈，所以看上去视觉上是更一体的，但功能的确有缩减。无线充电版本则保留了 4 ANC 上的盒身扬声器和无线充电线圈。盒身的开盖手感完全一致，有轻度的弹性反馈。USB-C 口的做工细节有一些变化，具体可以看图。配对也还是通过敲击正面两下调取，隐藏式 LED 灯也完全一致。 USB-C 口的工艺并不一样 耳机本体在盒内固定得还是相当稳的，只是从四代以来都一直存在的不太方便取出的情况也一并延续了下来，如果你和我一样手指头偏粗，那么需要习惯一下这个过程。耳机是典型的短柄 pods 式造型，从外观上跟四代没有任何区别，但是按照 Apple 发布会上讲到的，应该是内腔做了新结构来改善单元通气量。依然是和四代完全一样的比较饱满的长扁圆腔体，纵向上有所拉伸，开口位置仍然有所偏置，而非 AirPods 3 时代（也是当下大部分半入耳 TWS）采用的比较规矩的开口。在合理的佩戴下，漏音和漏气都控制得比较好。 实际佩戴下来我们也没有感知到跟 AirPods 4 系列的差别，都是相对贴合且佩戴压力较低的状态，对于大部分中大耳廓用户来说，AirPods 4 / 5 都应该有比常规半入耳形态更加扎实稳定的佩戴感受，常规强度的运动也不至于容易掉落。而小耳廓用户依然建议先试戴再做决定，由于两代外观一致，如果之前能够佩戴好 AirPods 4 系列，5 也不必担心。 相较于 AirPods 4 的 IP54 防尘防泼溅，AirPods 5 全系和 Pro 3 一样都是耳机本体与充电盒均支持 IP57 级别防尘防水，升级显著，现在它们在最深 1 米的水下停留时间最长可达 30 分钟，一般运动场景和小雨等也就用起来更加放心一些。 操作与软件端功能 | Control & APP AirPods 5 的机身操作依然依靠捏动柄部的触控区域进行，识别区域有专门的凹槽用于盲操。操作反馈的提示音比较清晰，反应迅速。可以识别单次、双次、三次按压以及长按操作。四代阉割了上下滑动操作，而五代加了回来，可惜只有那个五小时续航、带无线充电的版本支持，真是「等级森严」。好在，对于 AirPods 系列的操作识别准确度与识别效率，你不必担心，它仍然是非常跟手、相当准确的，提示音音量以及佩戴识别的表现都是行业第一梯队的顶尖水平。 在 iOS 27 更新之后，现在你可以通过设置实现更加复杂的功能设置，它依然保留了个性化音量、对话感知等功能，也可以开关人耳检测和进行空间音频的个性化，并且自定义操作逻辑等。头部动作的感知表现依然好用，现在也有了作为相机遥控器使用的设置项。 对，在我们手上的没有无线充电支持的版本中，苹果不光没有提供充电盒上的扬声器，连精确查找都阉割了…… 你只能购买那个定价 1149 元的无线充电版本才能获得精确查找。那么就 999 这个版本来说，它辅助查找的提示音全靠耳机发出，在盒外时这个音量其实还好，安静室内能够比较容易察觉到，但是稍微嘈杂一点的地方就不好说了（但仍比大多数依靠耳机发声辅助...

items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 2 Nov 2026] Title: Predictive gains, causal losses: why interventional competence cannot be learned from data alone View a PDF of the paper titled Predictive gains, causal losses: why interventional competence cannot be learned from data alone, by Marcus Thomas View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Retaining predictive gains can require persistent errors in a model's response to interventions. For deterministic predictors with finite second moments under squared-error loss, any observational advantage over the best predictor using only an outcome's direct causes requires dependence on other inputs, regardless of the learning rule. When admissible interventions vary inputs while preserving the worldly outcome, this dependence yields a positive lower bound on root-mean-square intervention-response error. We identify conditions under which population gradient updates introduce this dependence from a parent-only baseline or damage a previously correct mechanism through shared parameters while improving other predictions. These dependencies can also make model behavior vary with how the same intervention is realized. We characterize interventional alignment through a common output mapping across internal states and physical processes realizing the same intervention target and relevant context. Correction is limited by the causal hypotheses currently admitted within inquiry. The relevant hypothesis class comprises these causal alternatives, rather than the function class the computational system could in principle represent. For predictions restricted to these alternatives, interventional mean error cannot fall below the best approximation they permit, whether evidence is observational or interventional. Reducing error below a positive limit requires admitting better hypotheses, which may entail revising the causal variables, mechanism structure, or intervention interpretation. Interventional criticism constrains replacements without determining them. We...
