items.full_text_snippet: Political groups both supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections and shape the future of AI regulation. That spending produced mixed results, with some of the most heavily backed candidates losing their races. On the industry side, two AI-focused political action committees (PACs) that raised and spent money to influence the elections — American Mission and Building the Future — collectively spent $4.8 million to back South Carolina Senate candidate Darlene Graham, who lost. American Mission is the Republican spending arm of Leading the Future (LTF), a broader political group backed by OpenAI President Greg Brockman and the VC firm Andreessen Horowitz. American Mission also spent more than $500,000 apiece supporting Republican House candidates Aaron Flint in Montana and Laurie Buckhout in North Carolina, both of whom lost. LTF’s Democratic spending arm, Think Big, had better luck backing Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz, who won reelection. Groups advocating for stronger AI safeguards also saw mixed results. Public First, which is backed by Anthropic, supported several Republicans who lost through its affiliated PAC, but had more success backing Democratic candidates. It also contributed $3 million to a PAC supporting California state Sen. Scott Wiener, who was leading his race at the time of publication. Meanwhile, Guardrails Alliance , a group that has sought to make taking money from AI companies a political liability, spent more than $1 million apiece opposing two candidates who lost: California Rep. Jimmy Gomez and Montana’s Flint. It also spent $300,000 supporting Angela Gonzales-Torres, who defeated Gomez. It’s difficult to separate the impact of AI-related spending from the broader Democratic wave that swept Tuesday’s elections. items.full_text_snippet: On Tuesday, Apple rolled out a potentially controversial set of Audio Intelligence features into testing with the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3. The betas bring four new AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes. After just a day with Apple’s Siri Recaps feature on my Apple Watch, I can already see how its value may ultimately outweigh any creepiness factor that comes from the AI-powered audio recording and summarization it provides. However, I also see areas where AI-assisted note-taking can go too far, capturing things that aren’t worth remembering, and where there’s room for improvement. The first two, sound and song detection, don’t represent potential privacy concerns; they are designed to detect either important sounds — like an alarm or doorbell — or identify a song using Shazam’s technology. The former helps deaf and hard-of-hearing users navigate the world, and the latter is something we’ve already done with our iPhone for nearly two decades now. It’s the two other features, Live Rewind and Siri Recaps, that have raised concerns. The features record and then transcribe or summarize the conversations happening with and around the Apple Watch’s owner. Live Rewind lets you go back to see what was said in the past 15 seconds, while Siri Recaps summarize audio throughout your day, saving notes of the important things that were said. Image Credits: iPhone screenshot by TechCrunch Apple has taken care to ensure the privacy of these AI features by processing the audio and running AI models on-device, when possible, and by not identifying speakers, storing raw audio files, and redacting private information, like government ID numbers or personal account information. items.summary: The years-long wait for access to the grid and new turbines is causing data center builders to turn to an unusual, less-efficient and less environmentally friendly solution: once-discarded jet engines.
items.full_text_snippet: Stuck in years-long lines for grid connections and new turbines, some AI data centers are making their own electricity with converted jet engines, the New York Times reported Tuesday. The engines, pulled from retired aircraft and rebuilt to burn natural gas, aren’t anyone’s idea of a permanent power plant. But they’re another sign of how far power supply has fallen behind the AI buildout. For companies stuck in those lines, the main draw of converted jet engines is how quickly the engines can be up and running. “It’s all about getting power as fast as possible,” Rystad Energy analyst Audun Martinsen told the Times. With jet-powered units, “they can have a data center running in 24 months,” he said. Hooking up 100 megawatts to the grid in Northern Virginia, by comparison, takes about seven years , according to the International Energy Agency. Most power capacity is expected to come on by 2031, an executive at Mitsubishi Power, one of the world’s top makers of power generation equipment, told Bloomberg last week . In some cases, these delays are already costing some data center operators business. Last month, Microsoft pulled out as the anchor customer for Nscale’s data center in Loughton, England, after the local utility said it couldn’t deliver enough power until the early to mid-2030s. Elon Musk’s xAI is among the companies already using the engines, having installed eight converted jet-engine turbines in Mississippi to help power its Colossus 2 data center in Memphis, the Times reported, citing state permits and satellite imagery. The units come from ProEnergy, which rebuilds a GE engine commonly found on Boeing jets. In 2025, OpenAI followed Musk’s lead with gas turbines at its first Stargate site in Abilene, Texas. Crusoe, a Denver-based startup that builds AI data centers, is constructing that Abilene campus and ordered 13 of ProEnergy’s converted units in April. The addition of the new tab suggests that Netflix wants to make its growing library easier to navigate while shifting discovery away from an experience where users are endlessly scrolling through titles toward a more personalized and AI-powered experience. Netflix says AI Discover is powered by a new intelligence layer it’s been building that responds to what users tell the platform in real time and keeps learning. Image Credits: Netflix Once users pick a theme, they’ll see matching recommendations. They also have the option to select more specific themes so they can keep searching until they find something they’re interested in, or choose the “something different” option to start over. items.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up
items.summary: Apple's new App Store rules will require 18+ ratings for dating apps and AI companions that offer sexual or romantic content.
items.full_text_snippet: Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday. The new rules follow other changes the company has made to better protect minors, which include the rollout of its age assurance technology globally and more parental controls and child safety features . While most major dating services typically restrict their platform to adults, Apple’s new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating. Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said. It’s perhaps more interesting how this rule could impact AI companion apps, or those where such functionality is one of many features. Often targeted at younger people, Character.AI, Replika, and other AI apps let people create AI companions, including friends, lovers, boyfriends and girlfriends, and other fantasy characters. xAI last year also launched 3D animated AI companions that allowed users to unlock NSFW capabilities . As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally . In addition to “dating and relationships,” apps will also need to indicate if they are sharing the real-world locations of a user with another person or group as part of their functionality. Any app doing so raises obvious privacy concerns, especially if the user wasn’t aware that their location was being shared. The company noted that in Brazil, apps that provide location-sharing features for families can request an official rating from the government’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP/Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública), instead of being required to list them with the A16 rating, as the local law requires.

items.full_text_snippet: In late October, a slew of major cybersecurity issues came to light. But none were bigger than the so-called PHP2Shell vulnerability , which put a plethora of websites, including those of NASA , Wikipedia , the White House, and all other sites that run on Wordpress or Drupal (among others) at risk of exploits capable of both reading sensitive data and running malicious code on the host server. As far as anyone is aware, disaster has been averted: The hack was discovered by cybersecurity researchers who reported it to the PHP Foundation, and a patch was released before any bad actors got their hands on the exploit. However, PHP2Shell may be the canary in the coal mine, serving as a warning sign for what’s to come in the age of AI. “One of the things we’re witnessing now is that all the legacy software that was written by humans over the last 40 years is being exposed,” says Matt Suiche , AI security research lead at the cybersecurity startup Tolmo . “Now it is time for the technical debt to be paid off.” PHP Legacy Bug and Memory Errors PHP, which originally stood for “personal home page,” is a programming language created back in 1994 and largely used by legacy sites. The bug underlying the PHP2Shell vulnerability was reported to the PHP Foundation as far back as 2024. The bug caused a common type of issue called an out-of-memory error, in which the amount of memory allocated to a piece of data is too small to hold the data. Normally, this type of error causes the program to crash—an unpleasant but not inherently dangerous result. And so the bug remained unaddressed. “If you look at any at any point of time, there will be a bunch of bug reports that are waiting to be fixed, which are just crashes. Most people don’t take them very seriously,” says Suman Jana , an associate professor of computer science at Columbia University . “It’s just that it’s a lot of very specific reasoning that is painful to do. And AI, I think, has done a very good job at that.” –Suman Jan...

items.full_text_snippet: Our Residential Proxy Observatory , launched earlier this week, is a first-of-its-kind interface that gives researchers a global view of residential proxy and anonymized internet activity. While our team was looking through it, we noticed residential proxy exit activity on AS2650 . AS2650 is registered to the Executive Office of the President, the federal agency that hosts the White House network. Residential proxy services sell access to everyday devices, letting customers send traffic through them so it appears to come from that device's network. Confirmed residential proxy activity observed from the White House network, October 5 to November 3, 2026. What we observed From October 5 to November 3: Our residential proxy enumeration pipeline exited through the White House network 236 separate times . Those exits came from 6 addresses , on 26 of the 30 days . 28 separate residential proxy services were able to exit through this network. To make sure this was not a fluke, we checked these addresses against other residential proxy detection services, such as Spur and Synthient. Their public IP context pages independently identify these addresses as residential proxy exits. This is public access. Anybody can obtain it by signing up to a public residential proxy service, paying a few dollars and sending requests through it. We did not selectively target this network or try to make our probes exit from it. We caught this by chance, simply by requesting global rotating access through these services. Why this is concerning Most of the activity happens in the evening, Eastern time: about half of it falls between 5 p.m. and midnight, and almost none happens in the early morning. That pattern suggests a person rather than a public guest Wi-Fi network: someone regularly on the White House network late into the evening, whose device is infected with a proxy SDK. items.title: Hacking the Xbox 360 Hypervisor Part 3: Bad Update Improvements
items.summary: HN 热门讨论（14 points, 2 评论）by muricula
items.full_text_snippet: Welcome to part 3 of the Hacking the Xbox 360 Hypervisor blog series. In this part I’ll go over what happened after I released the PoC for Bad Update, and how it went from taking ~20 minutes with a ~30% success rate to being near instantaneous with a near 100% success rate. If you haven’t already I highly recommend you read (or at least skim through) part 1 and part 2 as this post will reference a lot of the material discussed there. This part will be very short but will catch you up for part 4 which covers the peer pressure exploit and will be out soon. Rock Band Blitz In the months following the release of Bad Update v1.0 there were two major improvements made to it by others. The first by “ihatecompvir” and “ InvoxiPlayGames ” is a new game save entry point in the demo version of Rock Band Blitz (RBB) called DaTArrest . The demo version of RBB is a package file that’s normally downloaded from the Xbox Live store for free and saved to your console’s HDD or memory unit. When the Xbox 360 got support for using USB sticks as storage devices all of the packages signed to boot from the HDD or memory unit were grandfathered in to also boot from USB storage devices. This means the RBB demo package can be copied to a USB stick as a normal file and launched on any console on a software version that supports it. By exploiting some memory corruption vulnerabilities in the game’s DLC parsing code they were able to craft a game save file that when loaded would bootstrap the Bad Update stage 2 ROP chain and begin the hypervisor exploit chain. Using RBB as an entry point we no longer needed the Tony Hawk American Wasteland game disc. Running the Bad Update exploit was now as simple as copying some files to a USB stick, plugging it into your console, and launching Rock Band Blitz from the dashboard. items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 虎鲸文娱“鲸锐AI”平台正式上线，AI视频单分钟成本节省30%以上 量子位的朋友们 2026-11-04 16:49:12 来源： 量子位 11月4日，虎鲸文娱集团打造的行业首个AI影视制作与管理平台“鲸锐AI”正式上线。 11月4日，虎鲸文娱集团打造的行业首个AI影视制作与管理平台“鲸锐AI”正式上线。鲸锐AI平台聚焦AI视频制作过程精准可控、银幕级质感成片交付、成本可管理三大目标，集成了市面上50余个主流AI视频生成模型与10余个自研模型，无限画布支持千级节点、百人实时协同创作。通过鲸锐AI平台的精准控制和流程优化，AI视频单分钟成本较传统AI生成方式可节省30%以上。 即日起，鲸锐AI平台官网（www.jingruiai.cn）开放全员注册，创作者无需订阅会员、积分即充即用。此外，用户在鲸锐AI平台的团队席位不限人数，避免由于团队人数增减带来的不必要席位成本，创作者团队的使用门槛进一步降低。 “对虎鲸文娱而言，鲸锐AI的正式上线是平台与新生代AI创作者共建文娱产业新基建的起点。”虎鲸文娱集团CTO杜颜龙表示，“接下来，鲸锐AI平台会在众多真实项目中持续打磨，我们期待更多专业团队把更严苛的要求带进来，和我们一起定义AI影视的专业标准。” （鲸锐AI官网页面） 让“抽卡”精准可控，AI视频单分钟成本节省30%以上 今年以来，AI生成内容加速进入大众视野。国家广播电视总局披露的数据显示，今年前8个月全国上线微短剧43万部，AI生成类占比超过九成。当画面生成不再是稀缺能力，能否按照专业标准稳定交付一部完整作品，正成为AI影视工业化的分水岭。 针对AI创作中普遍存在的反复生成、难以复现的问题，鲸锐AI平台将场景、人物表演、摄像机、虚拟片场和光影调节做成五类精控套件，配合35类工具、300余项精控能力，覆盖镜头、表演、光影、站位、场景编辑等创作环节，让创作者的每一镜意图都可以被精准表达、逐镜复现和持续微调，从“碰运气黑箱抽卡”转向“有意图地做选择”，减少无效返工。 据用户实测，在同一人、同场戏、同时长的对比条件下，鲸锐AI平台的视频制作时长可缩短40%至60%。 （鲸锐AI平台聚焦制作过程精准可控） 成片质量上，鲸锐AI平台通过AI人脸修复、9种真人影视质感增强模式、AI绘景以及自研超分与HDR方案，将AI素材提升至银幕与大屏级水准，可直出4K、60帧、10bit、HDR规格内容。 据平台实测，与传统的“导出—后期—回传”处理流程相比，鲸锐AI平台的超分直出方案可节省约65%的成本。 （鲸锐AI平台可实现银幕级质感成片交付） 专业制片流程也离不开精细化的成本管理——鲸锐AI平台支持按集、按场、按团队、按项目核算制作消耗，成本全程可追溯。 相较使用提示词、单模型的传统AI生成方式，通过鲸锐AI平台的精准控制和流程优化，AI视频单分钟成本可节省30%以上。 （鲸锐AI平台精细化成本管理模式） 适配真实生产环境，无限画布支持百人实时创作 杜颜龙介绍，鲸锐AI平台是从专业影视制作的真实生产环境中打磨而来，测试期间已支持百余部项目的落地生产，覆盖剧集、少儿、动漫、商业广告等全品类内容。为了更好地满足团队协作需求，鲸锐AI平台的无限画布支持千级节点、百人实时创作，可按项目、分集、分场和角色组织生产，并将数字资产、提示词与工作流统一沉淀，为长周期、多工种的影视内容项目提供组织保障。 据了解，在鲸锐AI平台正式上线前，多家制作团队与创作者已在实际项目中深度使用。多位参与内测的专业影视创作者反馈，从前期的可视化分镜，到制作中的资产管理，再到后期的超分与补帧，鲸锐AI平台能够提供覆盖全流程的专业支持，把导演想象的画面迅速呈现出来，让创作者能把更多精力放回镜头表现和故事叙述上，并且迭代快、周期短、成本更低。 业内知名制作公司时光坐标的负责人将鲸锐AI平台比作“一条串起来的线”，从场景编辑、角色资产到超分增强可以在同一页面完成，沟通与返工明显减少；九万里影业的负责人则表示，同一段描述下，鲸锐AI平台能更加自然地还原景深、材质与环境光的层次，机位与光感“基本能把脑海中的构图翻译成画面”。 “工具的价值，最终要由作品来证明。”杜颜龙表示，“我们希望鲸锐AI平台托住的不只是效率，更是每一位创作者对作品的认真——让懂镜头、懂表演、懂叙事的人，在新的创作方式中被放大，而不是被消耗。” （鲸锐AI平台四项首发权益） 本文由虎鲸文娱提供，量子位获授权转载，观点归原作者所有。 版权所有，未经授权不得以任何形式转载及使用，违者必究。

items.title: 智己LS8纯电版背后：8年研发底盘，两大厂联合开发电池
items.summary: 两位CTO，关起门来吵架
items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 智己LS8纯电版背后：8年研发底盘，两大厂联合开发电池 杰西卡 2026-11-03 20:57:35 来源： 量子位 “我们的电池有点贵，有时还贵不少。” 宁德时代CTO高焕，竟然亲口承认了自家电池的价格问题。 最近在智己LS8 NEO纯电版发布会后的媒体群访中，谈起宁德时代电池为什么贵，高焕非常坦诚地回答了这个问题。 不过，贵归贵，车企提起要求来，可是一点也不客气。 坐在他身边的智己汽车CTO项娇，就是一个典型例子。 高焕透露，两人相识多年，为了产品性能和技术规格，有时甚至会关起门来吵一吵。 比如，智己希望将93度电池的容量提升到103度，重量却不能增加；还要求超快充性能更好，但又不能过多占用整车热管理资源。 这意味着，宁德时代不仅要提高能量密度，还要进一步降低电池内阻，有些指标甚至需要再降低10%—20%。 容量、重量、充电速度、安全性、寿命，每一项都要兼顾。 而为了满足这些要求，双方的研发团队不得不反复磨合。 不过，谈到最终的技术路线，两位CTO的态度却高度一致： 专业的事，交给专业的人做。 这句话放在当下的新能源汽车行业，倒是别有一番意味。 过去几年，越来越多车企宣布自研动力电池，希望将这项核心技术掌握在自己手中。 智己却选择继续深化与宁德时代的合作，甚至将全系搭载宁德时代电池，作为LS8 NEO纯电版的重要卖点。 在这场群访中，两位CTO也把这条路线背后的技术考量，讲得更加具体。 两位CTO，关起门来吵架 一块电池，要造到什么程度才算好？ 站在电池厂和整车厂的角度，答案未必完全一致。 对于宁德时代来说，电池必须在能量密度、充放电性能、安全性和寿命之间取得平衡，还要兼顾生产成本和大规模制造的一致性。 而智己作为整车厂，需要考虑的问题更加具体：电池装在车上占多大空间、增加多少重量、留给其他部件多少热管理能力，以及最终能让用户获得多少续航。 双方的研发分歧，恰恰出现在这些具体指标上。 高焕举了一个例子。智己希望电池容量进一步提升，提出了103度电池维持93度电池重量的研发要求。 看起来只是多了10度电，但要在重量基本不变的情况下提升容量，就必须进一步提高电池系统的能量密度。 对一台大型纯电SUV而言，这项要求尤其重要。 智己LS8 NEO纯电版车长超过5米，还搭载了大量舒适性配置、智能驾驶硬件和全线控底盘系统。电池容量增加固然可以提升续航，但如果整车重量随之大幅增加，又会影响能耗、操控和底盘表现。 因而，在有限的重量空间里争取更多电量，成为双方需要共同解决的问题。 另一个难点，则是超快充。 高焕透露，智己希望进一步提升充电性能，却又不能把整车制冷能力全部分配给动力电池。 这就对电池本身的热管理能力提出了更苛刻的要求。 一项重要的优化方向是降低内阻。 按照高焕的说法，双方讨论过程中，智己曾要求在原有基础上将内阻进一步降低10%—20%，以减少充放电过程中的发热。 高焕对此的总结是，双方其实一直在性能、安全、寿命、能量密度、环境适应性和成本之间反复寻找平衡。 这样的联合研发，最终也体现在LS8 NEO纯电版搭载的两套电池方案中。 其中一套是93度黄金高效电池，采用磷酸铁锂体系。 磷酸铁锂电池在成本、安全性等方面具有自身优势，但低温环境下的性能表现、剩余电量估算等问题，一直是用户关注的重点。 这一次，双方将研发重点放在了电池管理系统与整车控制的协同上。 高焕透露，在低温场景下，团队对SOC估算算法进行了优化。 按照其介绍，行业相关估算误差水平通常约为5%—8%，而智己与宁德时代联合开发的这套方案，有信心将误差控制在2%—3%。 换句话说，改善的并不只是仪表盘上的一个数字。 尤其是在冬季、低电量等场景下，电池SOC估算越准确，车辆剩余续航的显示也就越有参考价值，能够降低电量预估不准带来的使用风险。 此外，两家企业还对充放电算法、能量回收和热管理进行了协同优化。 高焕介绍，经过优化之后，电池功率输出能够更加平滑，减少过去台阶式的功率变化；车辆加减速过程中的能量回收能力，也得到进一步改善。 这些变化涉及电池与整车控制策略之间的配合，很难单靠更换电芯来完成。 一套是103度单晶超能电池。 这套方案更加注重能量密度与整车重量之间的平衡。 高焕特别提到，LS8 NEO纯电版搭载了丰富的座舱和舒适性配置，这些都会增加整车重量。 因此，电池系统必须在提供更高容量的同时，尽可能控制重量，让底盘性能得到更好的发挥。 一套侧重成本、效率和日常使用体验，一套进一步提升能量密度，两种方案背后都有整车与电池共同开发的考虑。...

items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 苹果被曝的新产品，中国央企8个月前已装进公共卫生间 量子位的朋友们 2026-11-03 14:29:11 来源： 量子位 近日，彭博社记者马克·古尔曼（Mark Gurman）爆料，苹果公司正在研发一款“不录制视频”的智能家居摄像头，代号为J450，通过AI分析环境向用户推送文字描述，从而保障隐私安全。该消息一出，迅速在国内外科技圈引发关注和讨论。然而，据报道早在今年2月，中国电信人工智能研究院（TeleAI）就已推出类似产品——基于其自主研发的“新一代通信网”智传网（AI Flow）打造的面向公共安全领域的“TeleAI隐私摄像头”，目的是既能对风险行为实时预警，又能保障用户隐私安全。 TeleAI宣称其隐私摄像头可装在“公共卫生间”这种私密场景，在不存储、不传输原始视频画面的前提下，能够对打架、吸烟、跌倒等违规和异常行为进行识别和预警。该产品由中国电信集团CTO、首席科学家、中国电信人工智能研究院（TeleAI）院长李学龙教授带领科研团队自主研发，背后是智传网（AI Flow）的端云协同推理架构及家族式同源模型等核心技术，在采集瞬间就完成抽象特征向量的提取，自动剥离人脸、衣着等隐私细节，同时即刻销毁原始画面，从源头对隐私信息进行脱敏处理。 近年来，以校园霸凌为题材的影视作品揭示了隐秘角落中的极端行为，让隐私与安全成为只能二选一的艰难抉择。李学龙教授在谈及隐私摄像头的研发初衷时表示：“公共安全是国家安全和社会稳定的基石，是人民生命安全的重要保障。我们发展人工智能，目标要坚持从源头上防范化解重大安全风险，真正把问题解决在萌芽之时、成灾之前。智传网AI Flow的‘词元流’能够免除对原始视频画面的存储与传输，并通过文字、风格画等多种形态精准传递对危险行为的描述与提示。这不仅实现了隐私保护与安全预警的统一，也为视频监控开拓了全新范式。” TeleAI智慧看护助手产品展示图 当然，TeleAI隐私摄像头不只应用于公共卫生间，还能在老人独居的家庭或养老机构发挥重要作用。例如，当老人如厕、洗澡时跌倒，或突发急症无法行动、挥手求救，TeleAI隐私摄像头会识别到异常状况，并在5秒内向其家人或看护发出告警。据了解，TeleAI还推出面向养老、校园、医院场景的“TeleAI智慧看护助手”，软硬一体，实现一站式部署。该产品在设计上充分考虑了被看护人群的心理感受，采用了“烟感报警器”的吊顶外观设计，有效缓解“被监视”的抵触情绪。 隐私看护场景只是智传网（AI Flow）技术能力应用缩影之一。作为AI时代的“新一代通信网”，智传网（AI Flow）推动了通信范式从“比特流”向“词元流”的技术革新，既可以在隐私优先场景仅做语义理解，也可以在弱网环境下重建高清画面，广泛应用于赛事直播、应急通信、远洋作业等更多领域。在今年7月的世界人工智能大会（WAIC 2026）上，TeleAI就发布了智传网（AI Flow）覆盖“天、空、地、海”全域场景的落地成果，让“智能”迈向更广阔的应用空间。 本文由中国电信人工智能研究院提供，量子位获授权转载，观点归原作者所有。 版权所有，未经授权不得以任何形式转载及使用，违者必究。

stories.representative_title: Transformers Model Integration Contracts

factual_summary: On July 30, 2026, Transformers enabled PyTorch's scaled dot-product attention

items.title: Transformers Model Integration Contracts
items.full_text_snippet:
On July 30, 2026, Transformers enabled PyTorch's scaled dot-product attention
(SDPA) for T5. As a side effect, UMT5's decoder could attend to future tokens.
During training, it could peek at the answer it was supposed to predict.
Nothing crashed, and the bug stayed in main for almost two months. When we later replayed those commits, a small UMT5 model running on CPU flagged
it on every one of them. This post is about that model and the tests built
around it. Why bugs reach main Transformers supports over 750
model types, and its test suite is big: 88,000+ CPU tests on main, plus
200,000+ GPU tests in a daily run. Model tests are only part of it: we also
test pipelines, training, distributed execution, quantization and attention
kernels. The integration tests load real checkpoints and exercise the model's API on
real hardware. Running all of that on every PR would mean keeping a lot of GPUs
busy all day long, which isn't practical. By the time a scheduled run finds a
regression, it may already be in main. Our approach is to shrink the model instead. We build a fixture : a small
model made from the real checkpoint's configuration, with fewer and narrower
layers but every kind of layer it has, and its tokenizer and processor files
unchanged. It is published once, then reused. We run "fast integration tests"
against it on a cheap CPU runner. In our CPU study ,
the experimental UMT5 fixture used 66 MB of weights; the source checkpoint
is 1,227 MB. This also covers very large models: some don't fit on our standard GPU
runners, but their fixtures run on CPU. Model integrators already build tiny test models (Transformers' tiny-random-* checkpoints). We wanted a common recipe, and
checks that go beyond loading the model and running a forward pass. The UMT5
bug would have passed a forward pass just fine. Fixtures won't replace full integration tests, but on PRs they give us a
chance to catch bugs before they reach main. Introducing Model Integration Contracts transformers-...

items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 28 Oct 2026] Title: A Defense-Aware Explainable AI Framework for Feature-Level Vulnerability Analysis in Optimal Power Flow View a PDF of the paper titled A Defense-Aware Explainable AI Framework for Feature-Level Vulnerability Analysis in Optimal Power Flow, by S. M. Monzurul Hoque Chowdhury and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Optimal power flow (OPF) is a foundational analysis in power system operation, and inaccuracies in OPF decision-making can result in significant operational and security consequences. With the increasing adoption of machine-learning-based OPF surrogate models for real-time and large-scale applications, power system operation has become more susceptible to cyber threats, including data manipulation and false data injection attacks. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), particularly Shapley value-based approaches, has been employed to quantify the influence of input features on OPF outputs. Features exhibiting high influence are commonly interpreted as vulnerable. However, this interpretation neglects the role of attack detection mechanisms in the system, which typically monitor input-to-input relationships to detect anomalous behavior. Consequently, highly influential features may be readily detectable and may not represent the most vulnerable attack surfaces. To address this limitation, we propose a defense-aware explainable AI framework that explicitly incorporates attack detectability alongside operational impact. The framework integrates an OPF surrogate model representing input-to-output dependencies with a vanilla autoencoder representing input-to-input dependencies. Shapley-based explainability is applied to both models to construct a feature-level vulnerability metric. Empirical evaluation on IEEE test systems demonstrates that the proposed framework more accurately identifies security-relevant vulnerabilities than conventional OPF-surrogate-model-only explainability approaches. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 3 Nov 2026] Title: Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data View a PDF of the paper titled Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data, by Mohamed Gaha and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Accurate vegetation-encroachment assessment and risk mitigation require electric utilities to accurately locate and characterize distribution-network assets, including poles and power lines, and distinguish among medium-voltage, low-voltage, neutral, and telecommunication lines. Mobile and aerial Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds provide detailed 3D representations of these assets and their surroundings. However, power-line detection and reconstruction remain challenging because conductor returns are often sparse, incomplete, noisy, or occluded by vegetation. These challenges are especially significant in distribution networks, where lower pole heights and complex line configurations place conductors close to trees. In addition, mobile and aerial LiDAR datasets differ substantially in point density, viewing geometry, spatial coverage, and occlusion patterns. We propose a robust and automated reconstruction method combining scaled density-based clustering, robust polynomial fitting, and iterative fragment merging to recover individual conductors under severe data incompleteness and occlusion. Following semantic classification, the same reconstruction pipeline processes both mobile and aerial LiDAR data without modality-specific code or parameter tuning. The method is evaluated through degradation experiments, benchmarking, parameter sensitivity analysis, and large-scale validation. On the aerial dataset, it achieves 96.87% precision, 96.66% recall, a 96.76% F$_1$-score, and a geometric RMSE of 0.127 m. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 3 Nov 2026] Title: Reality and Perceptual Gaps in Expressive Swarm Robotics View a PDF of the paper titled Reality and Perceptual Gaps in Expressive Swarm Robotics, by Ali Imran and 9 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Moving robot swarms from simulation into the physical world can be difficult because small discrepancies in hardware, timing and communication can cascade across interacting robots and alter group behaviour. This challenge is known as the reality gap. When swarms operate in human environments, a second challenge emerges: a perceptual gap between what the swarm physically does and what human onlookers actually perceive. This study examines the same decentralised coordination code deployed across three robotic swarms-tabletop, aerial and human-scale mobile manipulators-during live artistic performances. We find that while the underlying algorithms executed reliably on all three platforms, physical embodiment drastically altered visible motion-distorting execution timescales by more than a factor of three and reshaping trajectory geometry. More importantly, audience surveys revealed that human interpretation does not mirror technical success: how observers attribute meaning (perceived purpose) and how they react emotionally (comfort versus threat) depend heavily on physical form. Meaning attribution and emotional responses did not vary together. Our results demonstrate that successfully transferring swarm software to physical hardware is insufficient for real-world deployment. Addressing the reality gap does not guarantee that the resulting collective motion will be readily interpreted by human observers. Swarms destined for human environments must be engineered not only for decentralised stability but also for the expressive physical dynamics through which humans interpret collective motion. items.summary: While it's not yet clear what kind of product the smartphone startup is cooking up, Nothing's CEO said the product is designed to leverage AI for productivity gains.
items.full_text_snippet: Nothing, the smartphone startup behind the distinctive Nothing Phone , is working on an AI product, but what it is remains unclear. On Wednesday, CEO Carl Pei posted on X that the company’s first “AI-native product” ships in December. “It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app,” Pei wrote. Pei has teased an AI-first device for some time and the company has also said that it plans to release a pair of AI-linked smart glasses, as well as earbuds with AI integrations. Pei’s description adds up to a screenless non-app that uses AI? He also calls it a “productivity tool.” Adding further mystique to the announcement, Pei seems to downplay any link to AI wearables. “The whole industry is hunting for its iPhone moment: the pendant, the pin, the glasses, the companion, some magical consumer device that makes AI part of everyone’s life,” Pei wrote. “I admire the boldness, but I read this moment differently.” No firm release date has been announced, but Nothing fans should know soon enough what the company has in store for them.

items.summary: Cybersecurity-focused Ballistic Ventures is seeking to raise $360 million for a new flagship fund and another $130 million for a separate investment vehicle.
items.full_text_snippet: Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity-focused venture capital firm co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein (pictured above, second from the right), is seeking to raise $490 million across two new funds, TechCrunch has learned through regulatory filings. The San Francisco-based VC firm filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund, matching the size of its previous fund raised in 2024, and another $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B. Neither fund had recorded any sales at the time of filing. The fundraising plans come as the growing use of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about more sophisticated cyberattacks. The rise of AI agents has also created new opportunities for cybersecurity startups and the venture capital firms backing them. Founded in late 2021, Ballistic Ventures’ founding team includes Schlein, former AT&T Cybersecurity president Barmak Meftah, and Roger Thornton, who co-founded security companies Fortify Software and AlienVault. The firm has backed companies, including Talon Cyber Security, acquired by Palo Alto Networks , and Pangea, bought by CrowdStrike , alongside startups such as Armadin , GetReal , Nudge Security, and Oligo Security. Ballistic’s ties to storied venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins, where Schlein spent more than two decades, help set it apart from rivals, a cybersecurity investor at another VC firm told TechCrunch. Its investment strategy, however, is similar to those of other cybersecurity-focused investors, including Forgepoint Capital and Ten Eleven Ventures, the person said. In 2022, Ballistic announced its $300 million debut fund and raised another $360 million for its second flagship fund two years later. It also raised about $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, per PitchBook data. The new Fund B is targeting a similar amount. U.S. cybersecurity startups raised...

items.full_text_snippet: DuckDuckGo is pitching itself to schools after Google created an opening for the alternative search engine. On Tuesday, Google told schools they could turn off Gemini , but it said shutting off its other AI features would cost schools Google Search , as well. DuckDuckGo, a company that focuses on user privacy by limiting data collection, clearly sees this as a moment to make inroads in education, where Google has historically dominated. According to figures Google has published in previous years, there are around 50 million Chromebooks in schools, used by students and educators, and its Google Classroom platform serves over 150 million users globally. On X , DuckDuckGo’s founder and CEO, Gabriel Weinberg, pointed to the company’s online documentation , explaining how schools can switch their default search engine to DuckDuckGo’s service instead, adding, “get in touch for help.” Meanwhile, DuckDuckGo’s chief public affairs officer, Kamyl Bazbaz, issued a stronger statement, writing , “Forcing AI on school children: how a monopolist behaves when they think people are powerless. Prove Google wrong.” In an email to TechCrunch, DuckDuckGo chastised Google for its decision, adding that Google could easily turn off Search’s AI features for schools if it wanted to. The company’s comments come as the American public is weighing how much AI they want to allow into their lives. As Tuesday night’s elections indicate, they don’t want AI data centers built in their towns. But using AI at work and school has become a common practice and requires a more nuanced discussion. Knowing that educators have struggled with AI, Google developed technology called “ Guided Learning ” that is meant to help kids learn by walking through problem-solving steps rather than just providing them with an answer. But educators are still asking for tools that let them remove AI from the learning process altogether. After the backlash on Tuesday, Google defended its decision, saying it was just respon...

items.full_text_snippet: Open source models are becoming more mainstream as enterprises, governments and startups alike rely on the promise of lower costs, more control, and more flexibility. But as increasingly capable models become more freely available, how do companies capture value? And with Chinese open models gaining ground, can American players keep up? On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Rebecca Bellan caught up with Irene Solaiman , Chief Policy Officer and SVP of Strategy at Hugging Face, about what startups need to know before building on open models, from choosing the right tools and infrastructure to navigating the trade-offs shaping the future of open AI. Listen to the full episode to hear about: Why startups, enterprises, and governments are switching to open AI models to cut costs, and when it makes less sense to use the most powerful models. Who makes money when the models are free to use, and whether the companies building them can capture the value they create. Why the U.S. may need deep-pocketed players like Nvidia to build an open frontier model that can compete with China’s, and what’s at stake if Chinese models become the global default. How recent attacks on open AI platforms are raising a difficult question: how do you keep an open ecosystem secure without closing it off? items.full_text_snippet: Everything is an AI scam now Whenever you watch a video on YouTube now, you will likely get an advert for a scammy product. In the past few weeks I've seen: A Tai Chi training program that promises to get you ripped like someone on steroids a superhero in 20 days. (Tai chi? Really?) Glasses that can adapt to any prescription (not how glasses work) and are also sunglasses sometimes A small USB stick that offers free Internet with no limits. An air con unit the size of a book that can cool any room - any room! - in 90 seconds. Endless mobile games that probably don't exist. This is leaking into other parts of the internet as well with adverts on the side increasingly looking like chum buckets. What annoys me is how little verification there is for any of this. It's like we have collectively decided that AI is inevitable, and the cost is the breakdown of truth itself. Scams used to be a bad thing and there used to be measures in place to stop them. Now they've escaped the spam filter and have run wild. As long as someone can create an unconvincing advert and pay, platforms will take anything. So we have all this poorly made junk which breaks the rules of reality, so what? Most people are aware its fake. The problem is the scammers only need to get through to a very small percentage of people to make their money back. It's not just adverts. items.full_text_snippet: 11 月 2 日，Raspberry Pi 宣布即日起上调部分 16 GB 内存产品的售价：16 GB 版 Raspberry Pi 5 上涨 80 美元，由 305 美元涨至 385 美元；Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 的各款 16 GB 版本均上涨 40 美元，具体价格见该产品页的产品简介。同样配备 16 GB 内存的一体式键盘电脑 Raspberry Pi 500+ 维持原价。16 GB 版 Raspberry Pi 5 于 2025 年 1 月推出时售价为 120 美元。 公司 CEO Eben Upton 在公告中表示，过去两年内存成本大幅上涨，公司此前已对受影响最严重的产品进行过多次选择性调价，并通过认证替代零件等方式扩大采购弹性。但 16 GB DRAM 缺少替代供应，加上其他零件持续短缺，公司不得不进一步上调部分高内存配置产品的价格。公司表示，此次调价仍未覆盖整个产品线，并将在内存成本回落后撤回涨价。 Raspberry Pi 建议用户按实际需要选择内存容量，可以改用低内存版本或更早的型号，也可以优化应用程序的内存占用；企业客户可联系公司寻求内存优化方面的支持。公司还提醒，部分不法商家借内存供应紧张高价倒卖产品或销售假冒产品，建议用户通过 Raspberry Pi 认证经销商按公司定价购买。 来源

projects.description: dsh-go — DeepSeek Harness 装进口袋：手机本机运行，也能遥控你的电脑。
projects.readme_excerpt:
安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。

1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。
2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。
3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。

仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。

本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。
projects.readme_intro: 简体中文  ·  English DeepSeek Harness 的 Android 客户端。手机上直接跑，也能遥控你电脑上的 DSH。 Trendshift 全语言日榜 #1 · 2026-10-30 Deepy 和鲸娘，陪你干活 干活时敲代码，做完来个空翻，等你确认会举手。打开「App 外显示」，它们还会跟你到桌面。 下载 DSH Go 从 GitHub Releases 或官网下载页获取最新版 APK，常见手机选 arm64 包。   感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱，我将尽快适配 iOS 和鸿蒙！大家 Star 点得越多，我适配得越快哦 hhh 第一次用可以先看 使用指南 ，遇到问题欢迎来 论坛和 QQ 群 。 手机上装过签名不同的早期测试包时不能直接覆盖安装，需要先卸载旧版；卸载会清空对话、Linux 环境和设置。 本机运行，也能遥控电脑 内置 Linux 环境，免 Root、免 Termux。电脑上的 DSH，也能一键切过去接着用。 插话、打断，过程自动收好 回复中途也能插话，排队的消息随时「立即发送」。做完的过程折叠成一行。 原生界面，也有网页版 和官方网页版一键切换，停在同一段对话，下次打开还是你上次用的那个。 分享卡、对话回放和链接 回复一键做成分享卡。整段对话生成链接，对方在浏览器里回放，链接端到端加密。 横屏与平板 横屏手机和平板重新排版：侧栏常驻，内容居中，弹出键盘也不挤。 主题配色与桌面图标 六套主题色，也能跟随壁纸或自选颜色。四款桌面图标，三种功能图标风格。 中文，也说 English 全部界面支持英文，在设置里切换，默认跟随系统。 手机操控 看屏幕、帮你点，三档确认随你选。敏感操作默认交还给你；放宽应用规则或解除限制前，请先了解风险。

projects.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
projects.readme_excerpt:
Install claude-mem for Grok Bot:

```bash
npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot
```

Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor.

**Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice):** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Disable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false`.

Install with a single command:

```bash
npx claude-mem install
```

The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the **claude-mem observer** with a **30 Day Free Trial**: memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. projects.description: Open-source skills for designing and reviewing software with AI agents
projects.readme_excerpt: Choose your coding agent. Install the complete plugin so its skills can read the reviewer prompts and document standards.
projects.readme_intro: Design with an elephant. Review with a goldfish. Install   ·  Quickstart   ·  Documentation   ·  Website Thousands of Google engineers use EGM, an open-source plugin, to draft specs with deep-context agents and stress-test them with zero-context subagents before writing code. **Elephant** holds your project context and drafts the specification. **Goldfish** reviewers examine the draft and referenced source material without the earlier conversation, helping expose unstated assumptions and blind spots. **You** make the architectural trade-offs and approve the specification before implementing. Use it when a feature needs design decisions before implementation. For a small, clear bug fix, use your normal coding workflow.
